articles.title: 4 Things Pochettino Must Fix At Manchester United
articles.summary: What do Mauricio Pochettino and Mary Poppins have in common?
articles.body: So there you have it. On Friday, Mauricio Pochettino shed his tears in an emotional press conference ahead of the United States men’s national team’s Concacaf Nations League two-legged quarterfinal series against Haiti, confirming what we all knew. The Argentinian is off to Manchester United with a desire to once again reclaim redemption as the 54-year-old manager – formerly at Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea — feels he has unfinished business in the Premier League. The job is clear. To help a muddled United in complete disarray, which finds itself in 18th place with eight points from the first 10 league matches. This is the club’s worst start in the top flight in 40 years, of course the arrival of a certain Alex Ferguson. How could you not like Pochettino? As a person, much like his mentor Marcelo Bielsa, he is brutally honest, direct and only demands an absolute hunger for the game, no matter your title or reputation. But Pochettino has something Bielsa never mastered, which is charisma. And it’s this charisma that must collectively work with his football on the pitch to resuscitate Man United. So as Pochettino becomes the first ever South American to take over the Red Devils as head coach, I see this situation with the club very much as the football version of "Mary Poppins." First we have the Man United fanbase, playing the role of the children, Jane and Michael Banks. All they want is love, attention and someone to care for their club. The Glazer ownership, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS — acting very much like George Banks — begrudgingly have hired once again someone who can fix this mess. Enter Mary Poppins. Mauricio Pochettino. The internal and external problems are as long as Jane and Michael’s list, but the hope is for their new manager to create magic and help them climb out of this conundrum. It will, however, take more than Dick Van Dyke to save this mess, but I think Mar—I mean, Pochettino – is up to the task. Here’s what Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix immediately. 1.Rebuild The Trust With The Fanbase It is a clear affirmation that the anger that stems from Man United is not on the head coach. It is on the ownership. We as analysts and pundits have talked about this endlessly and it’s extremely clear that there is a detached, hierarchical, strategic problem within the club. But the Glazer ownership, INEOS—they’re not going anywhere in the near future. Pochettino’s arrival, despite being a band-aid over a gunshot wound, needs to be about mending a broken relationship. I’ll get to the tactical outlook on the pitch in a moment, but the overall objective is for the Argentinian to arrive at Carrington and begin to set a precedent of trust between himself, the players, stakeholders and most importantly, the fanbase. He needs them on his side from the very first minute. The best way to do that is to speak to the press with honesty, to initiate a culture of blue-collar, hard-work effort on the training pitch, and to speak to the fans, about the fans, with the fans as much as possible. This is a Pochettino speciality. He connects with people better than most head coaches and it’s his job from day one, to place the first brick towards the bridge of trust and mutual respect. 2.Forget Perfection. It's 'Perfect Practice.' The late legendary basketball coach John Wooden would always say, "nothing will work unless you do," and I think that needs to be graffitied at the training facility in Carrington. Pochettino is known for his detailed -focused routines and gargantuan demands in training, but it all begins with accountability. He is a student of Bielsa and no one asks more of you as a person or athlete than the man whose nicknamed is "Loco." Pochettino is the same. And I think United’s number one responsibility is to heighten every asset of training. From eating habits to where you sit at lunch or how you warm up. Pochettino will demand perfection in practice, meaning that a few players will probably get a wake-up call when he arrives next Wednesday. 3.More Disciplined Defending What if I told you that the only teams in the Premier League who have conceded more goals are Ipswich Town and manager-less, bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace? United has given up 19 goals, which is just too much after 10 matches. Their defensive unit is in peril, and it’s not just about the individual, it’s a collective responsibility that lives within the midfield too. Pochettino, therefore, has to find a way to make United stronger at the back, beginning with a daunting trip to Anfield a week on Sunday. This isn’t a Pochettino strength per se, as his focus is high pressure and fluidity in the final third. But this has to be a major task for the Argentinian. 4.Veterans Into Leaders. Youngsters Into Believers. As I mentioned before, the mental issues with United are obvious, and it’s important to instill belief into the squad. I think about 21-year-old defender Lenny Yoro, for example, who desperately needs guidance. Or the obvious one, Kobbie Mainoo. He is such a talented midfielder, but what he has needed most is a proverbial arm around his shoulder. Pochettino has a fantastic history of developing and nurturing young players. England striker Harry Kane – who became a Tottnham legend under Pochettino's guidance – has alluded to this. Cavan Sullivan, the teenage U.S. star, constantly speaks about Pochettino’s belief in the young Philadelphia Union attacker. Younger members of United, therefore, need Pochettino more than ever. But I also think the veterans need it too, beginning of course with midfielder Bruno Fernandes and centerback Harry Maguire. It’s imperative for Pochettino to replace doubt with strength, and finger-pointing with accountability. I believe Pochettino can help this squad because this isn’t the same manager who left Chelsea in 2024. The Argentinian found a new version of himself with the U.S. and I’d like to think he arrives at Man United, not as a savior, but a warrior, who can help these down-and-out players pick themselves up again. Or, in retrospect, as Mary Poppins flying down from the skies with a magical umbrella, ready to save — not London — but the west side of Manchester.

articles.title: That Was Fast! Vikings HC Kevin O'Connell Reveals Kirk Cousins Timeline
articles.summary: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell announced that the recently acquired Kirk Cousins will start at QB in Week 10 vs. the Packers.
articles.body: That didn't take long! Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed in a press conference on Friday afternoon that recently acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins will start in the team's Week 10 road matchup against the Green Bay Packers (1 p.m. ET on FOX); the Vikings defeated the Packers at home in Week 1, scoring 29 consecutive points to get a 39-22 victory. "I cannot give him enough credit for coming in here with how he's gone about the week, both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said of Cousins. "It's been really impressive what he's been able to do with the command and just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. "And it's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed with, so exciting to start Kirk." Of course, Cousins' arrival in Minneapolis marks his second stint with the Vikings, as the four-time Pro Bowler played for the franchise from 2018-23 and for O'Connell from 2022-23. Minnesota acquired the 38-year-old Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday afternoon for a 2027 third-round pick. Across the nine starts he made for the Raiders this season, Cousins totaled 2,340 passing yards, 20 passing touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 97.1 passer rating, while completing 64.1% of his passes. After starting the season 0-6, the Vikings have lost back-to-back games. In the second of those two losses, a 23-6 defeat at home on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills, Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz tossed two interceptions, threw for only 81 yards and completed just eight passes. Wentz was starting in place of Kyler Murray, who's dealing with a hamstring strain and will be inactive Sunday, per O'Connell. articles.title: Dutch Romp Greece, Germany Cruises In UEFA Nations League Action
articles.summary: Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez and Germany boss Jurgen Klopp got some statement wins, respectively.
articles.body: The Netherlands routed Greece 7-0 in a statement Nations League victory to stay unbeaten under new coach Xavi, while Jürgen Klopp's Germany cruised to a 3-1 win over Serbia on Friday. That now sets up a decider between the two big-name coaches for first place in their group. Tijjani Reijnders scored a hat trick and Jurrien Timber had two goals in a rampant win for the Netherlands. Beaming and holding up three fingers, Reijnders celebrated a hat trick which came off a series of slick team moves to tear apart the Greek defense in Amsterdam. Crysencio Summerville got the Netherlands started with a sixth-minute opener before Reijnders scored three in the space of 21 minutes, Timber added two more and Donyell Malen a seventh. Germany is three points behind Group A2 leader the Netherlands before they play on Monday in Berlin. The top two in the group advance to the quarterfinals, with head-to-head record as the tiebreaker. The Netherlands, Germany and Greece are all able to qualify. Serbia is last after losing all of its five games. Germany Wins In Front Of Serbia's Sparse Crowd Goals from Florian Wirtz and debutant Brajan Gruda lifted Germany to its second win in five games with Klopp as coach after a slow start to his tenure. In driving rain, Germany was ahead after just three minutes when Serbia defender Srdjan Babic turned Germany forward Kai Havertz’s header into his own goal. It was 2-0 soon after when Wirtz flicked a rebound over goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, who had parried a shot from Havertz. Klopp’s experimental squad, with Freiburg winger Derry Scherhant but no place for Barcelona’s Karim Adeyemi, added a third when Leipzig's Gruda dribbled through the center of the Serbian defense to score Germany’s third. Babic canceled out his earlier own goal by scoring for Serbia on a rebound, but chances of a comeback were ended when Vanja Dragojevic was sent off for a reckless tackle on Joshua Kimmich's ankle. The 50,000-capacity Rajko Mitic stadium was almost empty because Serbia was supported by only 5,000 accompanied children and teenagers. That's because UEFA was punished the Serbian soccer federation for fans’ offensive behavior in the previous rounds. Swiss Promotion Bid On Track Switzerland is playing in the second tier of the Nations League for the first time, but its bid to rejoin Europe's elite stayed on course in a 0-0 draw with Slovenia, its closest rival in Group B1. Scotland won against North Macedonia 2-1. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Sean McVay Gives Injury Updates On Rams Stars Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie
articles.summary: Rams head coach Sean McVay provided an injury update on superstar defensive end Myles Garrett and All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie.
articles.body: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett expects to play Sunday despite missing practice, while cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable for their game at the Arizona Cardinals. Garrett was held out of practice on Friday after being limited earlier in the week because of a knee injury that caused him to miss seven games before returning to make three sacks with a forced fumble in the Rams’ 20-13 win at the Washington Commanders on Sunday. "He’s had a really good week," coach Sean McVay said. "Played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that. But we’re being smart with him." Garrett was largely pleased with his performance, in which he played 61.5% of the defensive snaps, apart from needing to build up his endurance and address what he felt was a slow get-off time. "I'm sure Next Gen or PFF or somebody would tell me it wasn't too bad," Garrett said. "It felt terrible to me." McDuffie is dealing with a back injury that forced him to miss the Rams’ third straight win last week, getting them over .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. McVay expressed optimism he would be able to play, provided McDuffie felt good coming out of Friday's workout. "He was rolling, you know, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said. The ongoing issues with the Rams’ two marquee offseason acquisitions are indicative of their larger injury crisis that has threatened a campaign that began with them as Super Bowl betting favorites. Los Angeles is so beat up that star wide receiver Puka Nacua was placed on injured reserve Thursday to free up a roster spot, a reversal from what McVay had indicated earlier in the week when he cited the limited number of IR slots remaining to be able to bring players back later in the season. "Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces," said McVay, while adding that nothing has changed with the timeline for Nacua’s return from knee and toe injuries. Safety Kam Curl is questionable with a toe injury, but McVay indicated he is likely to play. The same is expected for the Rams’ banged-up crop of tight ends, Colby Parkinson (ribs), Tyler Higbee (illness) and Davis Allen (oblique). All three are needed to supplement the passing game with top receivers Nacua, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back) on IR. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) and left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) were ruled officially out, as was previously announced. The Rams were upset by the Cardinals 18-16 on Oct. 18, giving up a last-minute drive which ended with Chad Ryland kicking his sixth field goal as time expired at SoFi Stadium. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Salah breaks Egypt scoring record, Tunisia lose to Libya in AFCON qualifier
articles.summary: Salah scored twice to take his international tally to 70 and surpass former captain Hossam Hassan’s record.
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah scored twice in Egypt’s 5-0 thrashing of Malawi in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on Friday, becoming the country’s leading all-time scorer with 70 goals.

The 34-year-old former Liverpool star left it late in Cairo to overtake Hossam Hassan, scoring with a far-post header in the 84th minute and from a penalty five minutes into added time.

Hassan was fired as Egypt coach last week, and replacement Ali Maher made a perfect start with goals from Nasser Maher, Omar Marmoush and Mohamed Hany building a 3-0 lead by half-time.

Egypt have seven points in Group B after three matches, three more than Angola, who host South Sudan on Saturday.

Achraf Hakimi, favourite to win a second successive African Footballer of the Year award next month, also bagged a brace as Group A pacesetters Morocco crushed Niger 5-1 in Casablanca.

Substitute Tolu Arokodaro scored twice within eight minutes as Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo to get their campaign back on track.

Tunisia suffered a shock home 2-0 loss to Libya, and Kenya scored in the final minute to snatch a surprise 2-2 draw away to South Africa.

Alhassan Yusuf put Nigeria ahead after just 103 seconds and Alphonce Msanga equalised on 32 minutes following a rare Tanzanian attack.

Arokodaro, scorer of six goals in his last five matches for Ajax Amsterdam, came off the bench for the second half and quickly made an impact.

His near-post back heel off a low cross put Nigeria ahead for the second time after 52 minutes, and as the match reached the hour mark, he struck again from close range.

An ultimately comfortable victory lifted the Super Eagles to six points after three rounds in Group L, one point behind Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday.

Nigeria back on track, Tunisia in trouble

Although bottom of the table with just one point, Tanzania are guaranteed a place at the 2027 AFCON as cohosts with Kenya and Uganda.

That means Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria and Madagascar must fight for one place at the 24-nation tournament, the first to be staged in East Africa since Ethiopia were the 1976 hosts.

Nigeria were in trouble after a 3-0 hammering in Guinea-Bissau two months ago, but now have a clear path to a tournament they have won three times.

Away wins over Tanzania on Tuesday and Madagascar in March, and a home win over Guinea-Bissau, also in March, will assure qualification.

Tunisia are in Group H, which includes cohosts and automatic qualifiers Uganda, and their record of reaching every AFCON tournament since 1994 is in peril.

A 2-0 defeat at home to neighbours Libya leaves them bottom of the table with just two points, and a venue switch two months ago means their remaining three fixtures are all away.

Ali Youssef converted a 44th-minute penalty for Libya, and Hamdou Elhouni, who once played for leading Tunisian club Esperance, doubled the lead in the 62nd minute.

Victory lifted Libya from last place to a share of the lead on four points with Uganda. Botswana and Tunisia have two each. Uganda host Botswana in Kampala on Saturday.

The Group D clash between South Africa and Kenya pitted two South African coaches against each other. Pitso Mosimane handles Bafana Bafana and Benni McCarthy guides the Harambee Stars.

Former Manchester United coaching staffer McCarthy was the happier at full-time after Ryan Ogam equalised in the final minute of regular time.

From a South African perspective, this was two points lost, although they remain on top with seven. Guinea have six, automatic qualifiers; Kenya, two; and Eritrea, one.

articles.title: Reijnders’ hat-trick fires Dutch to 7-0 rout of Greece, Germany beat Serbia
articles.summary: Netherlands’ 7-0 annihilation of Greece means the Germans will likely need to win on Monday to reach the quarterfinals.
articles.body:
Tijjani Reijnders netted a first-half hat-trick as the ⁠Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 in the ⁠Nations League on Friday, while Germany earned a 3-1 victory away to Serbia in the other Group A2 game.

The Dutch were 5-0 up at the break, with Crysencio Summerville putting the hosts ahead in the sixth minute before Reijnders ran ⁠riot and Jurrien Timber notched their fifth before half-time. Timber scored again just before the hour mark, with Donyell Malen netting the final goal.

Germany took a third-minute lead through an own goal, and Florian Wirtz added a second 11 minutes later. Brajan Gruda scored on his debut five minutes after the ⁠break before Srdan Babic pulled one back for Serbia, who finished the game with nine men.

The Netherlands are top of the standings on 11 points, and Germany moved level on eight points with Greece to leave the three sides battling it out for two quarterfinal places on Monday. Germany will host the Netherlands in Berlin while Greece host a Serbian side that has lost all five fixtures.

Greece and the Netherlands both came into the game unbeaten, but ‌the Dutch destroyed the visitors in a devastating display of attacking prowess.

The opening goal came after Greece lost possession close to their own area, before a poorly controlled ball by defender Konstantinos Mavropanos fell to Summerville and he slipped his shot past the keeper.

Joey Veerman threaded a pass through to Reijnders, whose strike found the roof of the net from the edge of the six-yard area in the 12th minute, and six minutes later he finished off Malen’s pass across goal.

Reijnders completed his hat-trick with a simple tap-in after Denzel Dumfries nodded the ball down in the six-yard box, and Timber netted from close range with Malen providing another assist.

Timber’s second came after Dumfries’ cross was pushed ⁠away by the keeper, and Malen got his well-deserved goal following some neat skill and a lay-off from ⁠Dumfries.

Jurgen Klopp had a difficult start to life as Germany’s manager , winning just one of his opening four games, also against Serbia.

Klopp had used his first international window to experiment with a 44-man roster split into two separate squads, but his chosen 11 put in a dominant display under heavy rain in Belgrade, especially in the ⁠opening half.

Germany went in front after a Kai Havertz header went in off Babic, and when Havertz had a shot parried away by keeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, Wirtz was there to convert the rebound.

Klopp’s side missed chances to ⁠finish off the game in the first half but looked well in control after Gruda’s ⁠solo goal.

Gruda collected Joshua Kimmich’s pass inside his own half, drove forward largely unopposed and drilled a low shot into the far corner from outside the area.

Babic’s goal gave Serbia hope, while Germany continued to attack. Kimmich had a goal ruled out for offside, and Derry Scherhant hit the post before Vanja Dragojevic’s red card in the 74th minute. Serbia had ‌another substitute, Andrija Zivkovic, sent off late on.

In Group B1, Switzerland earned promotion to League A thanks to a 0-0 draw in Slovenia, while Scotland earned a 2-1 win over North Macedonia thanks to a John McGinn double. Scotland captain Andy Robertson made a record-equalling 102nd ‌appearance, ‌drawing level with Kenny Dalglish.

Slovakia were held to a 2-2 draw at home by the Faroe Islands in Group C3, but the point was enough for the hosts to clinch promotion.

Iceland romped to a 5-0 win in Bulgaria to remain top of Group C4, with Andri Gudjohnsen providing a hat-trick.

articles.title: Aparece en Miami el Mercedes 'madrileño' de un ex piloto de Ferrari fallecido en un trágico accidente
articles.standfirst: Se trata de un Mercedes 300E 5.6 que a mediados de los años 80 era capaz de rivalizar en prestaciones con los Ferrari Testarossa y Porsche 911 Turbo
articles.summary: Se trata de un Mercedes 300E 5.6 que a mediados de los años 80 era capaz de rivalizar en prestaciones con los Ferrari Testarossa y Porsche 911 Turbo
articles.body: Curated pasa por ser uno de los concesionarios de coches de lujo que más piezas originales o de colección vende en Miami. Lo que encuentras en sus instalaciones siempre es raro por su escasez, además de que en ocasiones ha pertenecido a personalidades de todos los ámbitos y en todos los casos resulta sangrante para cualquier economía media. Lo que ha anunciado en esta ocasión es lo que, a simple vista, cualquier español de a pie podría encontrar en Wallapop: aparentemente, un Mercedes de los 80 de cuatro puertas con matrícula de Madrid. En realidad, un coche con un motor lleno de furia y un pasado en el que perteneció a un piloto de la escudería Ferrari. El coche en cuestión es un Mercedes 300E, pero con la firma de AMG y con un motor V8 de 5,7 litros con 32 válvulas, en lugar del 6 cilindros de 3,0 litros y 8 válvulas con el que se vendía de forma estándar. Para dar una idea de su potencial, basta decir que alcanzaba 300 km/h, por lo que era más rápido incluso que un Ferrari Testarossa que, en aquella época, era ya el icono de los coches deportivos. Su potencia de 360 CV y su par motor de 510 Nm también impulsaban de 0 a 100 en 5,8 segundos una masa total de 1.660 kg, que pisaba el asfalto con neumáticos que entonces parecían enormes y ahora nos parecen discretos: 215/45 R17 delante y 235/45 R17 detrás. Por fuera, el AMG parecía un coche algo tuneado, con suspensiones rebajadas, un paquete aerodinámico que incluía un alerón en la tapa del maletero y un spoiler frontal, llantas específicas y unos asientos deportivos firmados por Recaro. Pero nada que anunciara que, sobre el asfalto, le podía iba a hacer frente al citado Testarossa o al Porsche 911 Turbo. De hecho, también rivalizaba con el modelo italiano por lo que toca a precio, ya que el Tetarossa costaba al cambio unos 144.243 euros (unos 24 millones de pesetas), mientras que el Mercedes salía por unos 133.000 euros; nada que ver con los 75.252 (12 millones y medio, aproximadamente) que costaba entonces un Porsche 911 Turbo 3.3. El coche en cuestión fue propiedad de Michele Alboreto, un piloto de Fórmula 1 que corrió cinco temporadas con Ferrari y logró tres victorias con los bólidos rojos, y que por desgracia falleció en unas pruebas con un Audi de resistencia en 2001. Nada sorprendente, por tanto, que una figura del automovilismo se comprara un coche muy exclusivo. Lo que no encaja es la matrícula. La placa M-9818-IC se entregó en 1987, dos años después de que el coche tuviera la que sería su primera matrícula. Y esto da a entender que quizá Alboreto se desprendió del coche y lo compró alguien que vivía en Madrid. Lo curioso es que casi 40 años después el coche sigue con la misma matrícula pese a haber recalado en Estados Unidos. Hace dos años, el coche pasó por una profunda reconstrucción de su inyección mecánica KE Jetronic (era un poco problemática) y por revisión tanto del motor como de la transmisión automática de cuatro velocidades. Y no en cualquier taller, sino en uno de los mayores especialistas en viejos AMG de Estados Unidos. Todo se hizo elevando la factura de la operación de taller a 21.700 euros para que el coche volviera a rodar como el primer día. Curated no anuncia el precio que pide, pero es posible que su tarifa se aproxime a los 300.000 euros.

articles.title: Pacers hold off Knicks in NBA Cup thriller, Spurs rout Warriors
articles.summary: The New York Knicks look unlikely to advance to the NBA Cup knockout rounds after falling to the Indiana Pacers.
articles.body:
The shorthanded Indiana Pacers held off New York 106-104 on Friday to leave the Knicks’ bid for an NBA Cup repeat in tatters.

The Knicks won last year’s in-season tournament in what proved a curtain-raiser to their run to a first NBA championship since 1973 .

But after coming up short in their bid to erase a 14-point third-quarter deficit, the Knicks fell to 0-2 in Cup play.

They are not mathematically eliminated, but in three prior editions of the Cup, no team with two group-stage defeats has reached the knockout rounds.

Pascal Siakam scored 19 points to lead a balanced Pacers attack. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, Kelly Oubre Jr added 16, and Ivica Zubac and Andrew Nembhard chipped in 12 apiece to lead Indiana, who were again without injured star Tyrese Haliburton.

Jalen Brunson scored 33 points and handed out 11 assists for the Knicks, who tied it at 87-87 early in the fourth quarter, only for the Pacers to pull away again with a 15-2 scoring run.

The Knicks made one last push, cutting the deficit to two, but Karl-Anthony Towns – who scored 23 points and pulled down 15 rebounds – missed a potential game-tying basket with nine-tenths of a second remaining.

“Very proud of our team. We were pretty big underdogs coming into this game,” said Pacers coach Rick Carlisle, whose team outscored the Knicks 50-30 in the paint.

“Second half, it got difficult. New York is a championship team. They know how to make comebacks,” Carlisle said. “Our guys stuck together and kept fighting together.”

The Knicks are last in East Group B and will host the Cleveland Cavaliers and Miami Heat in their last two Cup group games.

In Miami, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo scored 37 points each to lead the Heat to a 133-121 victory over the Cavaliers.

Adebayo added 14 rebounds, and Davion Mitchell chipped in 22 points and 17 assists to help the Heat improve to 2-0 in Cup play – top of the group – and 6-6 on the season.

The San Antonio Spurs, who fell to the Knicks in last year’s NBA Cup final before losing to them in the NBA Finals, crushed the Golden State Warriors 123-85, their 11th straight victory pushing them to 2-0 in Cup play.

Stephon Castle scored 32 points and Victor Wembanyama added 12 points and 12 rebounds for the Spurs, who opened the game on an 18-0 run and led by as many as 43 against a Warriors team playing without injured superstar Stephen Curry.

LJ Cryer scored 20 points to lead the Warriors as none of the Golden State starters scored in double figures.

Veteran Draymond Green finished with four points and was assessed a flagrant foul for a shove from behind that sent Wembanyama crashing out of bounds midway through the second quarter.

In the last game of the night, the Los Angeles Clippers improved to 1-1 in Cup play – just 3-8 overall – with a battling 113-112 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Darius Garland sealed the victory with a three-point play with less than a minute remaining, driving for a layup that tied it at 112-112, drawing a foul and converting the free throw.

LA’s Brook Lopez scored 11 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter, and the Clippers withstood a 40-point performance from Oklahoma City’s two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander – who came up empty on two attempts in the waning seconds.

articles.title: Warner accuses Cricket Australia of ‘cover-up’ in ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: Former opener Warner was banned for a year for his involvement in the 2018 ‘Sandpapergate’ incident in South Africa.
articles.body:
David Warner blasted Cricket Australia’s handling of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal as “a cover-up” on Saturday, escalating a row that has torn apart the sport.

Former opener Warner, who was banned for a year over his part in the “ Sandpapergate ” incident in Cape Town, lashed out at what he claimed was “a shoddy investigation”.

“As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation,” he said on Instagram.

“If that’s correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?

“It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose, and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.

Festering wounds over what happened in the third Test at Cape Town were reopened this week when Usman Khawaja released his autobiography.

In the book, he alleged that the whole team knew about the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing.

A Cricket Australia probe concluded that only then-skipper Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were in the know, with all three sent home from South Africa in disgrace .

Starc, Hazlewood, Lyon and Pat Cummins all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan.

On Friday, Cummins, now the Test captain, held a lengthy news conference to rubbish Khawaja’s latest claims, calling them “ 100 percent wrong “.

In response, Warner accused him of throwing close friend Khawaja “under the bus”.

Starc also stated during the week that “we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field”. Hazlewood and Lyon have yet to comment.

Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening their investigation and, in a statement on Saturday, said all players had been given the chance to come forward.

“As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since,” a spokesperson said.

“Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players’ right to provide their own version of events.”

articles.title: Cameron Menzies: Scottish darts player sheds weight & embraces fitness after medical issues
articles.summary: Cameron Menzies has lost five stone and embraced fitness and different forms of therapy after medical issues threatened to upend his darts careers.
articles.body:
Cameron Menzies has lost five stone after hand surgery and a medical fright threatened to upend his darts career.

The Scot, 37, needed an operation for an injury sustained repeatedly punching a drinks table on stage following his first-round exit at the PDC World Championships last December.

And he made headlines during the summer after requiring medical attention during his World Matchplay encounter with Ross Smith, which he had to forfeit.

His dizzy turn was put down to high blood pressure caused by dehydration.

"I didn't know what it was, I looked at the board and I just felt like everything was spinning," Menzies told BBC Scotland.

"They took me off the stage, there were paramedics and first aid on site and they were taking my blood pressure and it was up to over 200, and they were going to phone an ambulance because that was like heart attack material.

"But as soon as they gave me a drink of water it dropped massively. They wouldn't let me leave the venue until they were quite happy with it and then when I came back up to Glasgow the next day I went to the Royal Infirmary and got bloods taken and stuff – it was just high blood pressure dehydration.

"I have got a little blood pressure machine now. I have been taking that as much as possible and everything has been fine.

"I just make sure I drink a lot more water. It was warm that day, I had a lot of TV stuff to do and I maybe didn't look after myself much because it had never happened before and hopefully never happens again."

Menzies upsets Van Veen to win second title of year

On his weight loss, Menzies elaborated: "My heaviest was 21-and-a-half stone, I didn't realise how big I was until I see pictures now and I am like, 'wow I was big'.

"It was for my health to try and lose weight because I had a thing last year with my heart so I went to the hospital and found out that I have got an ectopic heartbeat so my heart skips an extra beat.

"They told me to try and lose weight before they did anything with tablets, so thankfully it has dropped to a level where it is fine, I don't need tablets.

"I just usually do a 5k, I don't do many weights because then I can't throw darts but I just go for a jog. It is good for my physical health and it is good for my mental health, I never leave the gym feeling bad, I like doing it for that as well."

It is not just Menzies who has got the fitness bug, with a host of other top players seeing the benefits of being in good shape.

"You look at the players nowadays, most of them are starting to look after themselves now," Menzies added.

"Luke Humphries lost a power of weight, there have been a few more.

"Most of the hotels we stay in have got gyms and a lot of guys are just popping to the gym or they go on 5k runs. Even the commentators and the referees are doing it.

"The darts world is changing, I do think in the future you will get a lot more people looking like sportsmen rather than darts players."

How sports psychology & hypnotherapy have helped

Eleven months on from his hand injury, Menzies appears to have made a full recovery and has gone on to enjoy a solid season, winning two PDC ProTour titles this year.

He is preparing to compete at the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton this weekend, but feared he might never return to top level darts.

"At the start of the year I thought that could have been me because I had no feeling in my hands after the operation," he said.

"I was in a bandage for six weeks, and the first three or four months I couldn't feel a dart, so I am lucky.

"Obviously it was my own fault but I am lucky enough that I can still play at a good level.

"With the [Luke] Littler effect the prize money is good. I had a good job before as a plumber but the money in darts these days is life changing."

Up until relatively recently, the Ayrshire player often struggled to control his emotions on the oche, which clearly inhibited his undoubted talent.

The world number 26 has a calmer demeanour now - something that has been helped by his decision to embrace sports psychology and hypnotherapy.

"Every night I have got a track to listen to. The sport psychologist does the hypnotherapy treatment and at night you listen to him talking to you. He is just talking to your subconscious, the same thing every night when you go to sleep.

"I usually fall to sleep after 15 minutes - it is just talking to your brain really rather than yourself.

articles.title: Georgia Taylor-Brown wins in Dubai to move top of T100 standings
articles.summary: British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown moves top of the overall standings in the women's T100 series with her second victory of the season in Dubai.
articles.body:
British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings.

The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining.

Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event.

The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series , is aiming for her first T100 world title.

Taylor-Brown won her first T100 race - which includes a 2km swim, 80km bike ride and 18km run - in Spain in May and was third in Vancouver, Canada in August.

She hit the front in Dubai just under 4km into the run and opened a 30-second advantage before holding off New Zealand's Nicole van der Kaay to win by just 10 seconds, finishing in three hours 35 minutes and 19 seconds.

Derron, who took the lead in the overall standings with victory in Vancouver, was third in Dubai, finishing two minutes seven seconds behind Taylor-Brown.

Britain's Kate Waugh, the 2025 champion, was ninth, just ahead of team-mate Lizzie Rayner.

Waugh missed the opening two events of the season with a calf injury and is eighth overall heading into next month's Grand Final in Doha.

articles.title: ‘They just continue to show up’: How Minnesota football became family to a community shattered by a school shooting
articles.summary: A young boy was shot and killed in a 2025 school shooting that shook Minneapolis. A year later, the Minnesota football team has made his parents and friends family.
articles.body: PJ Fleck always has something to say. The University of Minnesota football coach is a fiery motivator equipped with acronyms and analogies, metaphors and mantras, for any situation. He’s known for his intensity. He is sometimes compared to the Energizer Bunny. He’s been seen wiping the blood from a player’s split lip across his own bald head after a recent hard-fought victory, inspiring the broadcast to declare that Fleck had “gone insane.” But last year, before a game against Michigan State, Fleck found himself facing a situation far bigger than football. He told his wife he had never felt more pressure to win. For the first time, maybe ever, Fleck worried intently about what to say. “If there’s one time in my life that I didn’t want to say the wrong thing,” Fleck told CNN Sports of the moment. “I’ve said a lot of wrong things after games. I didn’t want to say the wrong thing.” It’s a fear that stops so many people from saying anything, especially when nothing you could say will change a horrible reality. What can anyone say in the wake of a school shooting? Fleck didn’t want the luxury of staying silent, though, instead feeling an incredible sense of responsibility as a highly visible state employee and a deep well of empathy as a parent. In truth, he felt it was a calling to serve his Minneapolis community reeling from a tragedy in exactly this way. “I just wanted him to know that we’re here for the healing process – however, and as much as, you want us,” Fleck said. Jesse Merkel was not a University of Minnesota fan. In fact, as a college runner, he’d had a negative experience with their recruitment process and harbored a low-level grudge for a couple of decades. Plus Fleck always seemed like a bit of a showboat, especially compared to the deferential Minnesotans. Merkel’s impression of Fleck was that the coach was “able to cram 10 minutes of words into five minutes of conversation. … A little much at times.” But that was before. Before he knew PJ Fleck as a fellow father who had experienced unthinkable loss. Before everything changed and he learned far more deeply than anyone should ever have to what true generosity looks like because it comes in the wake of true evil. That was before Jesse Merkel’s son was killed in a school shooting at eight years old. ‘He was my mini-me’ Fletcher Merkel loved sports. “He would play tiddlywinks,” his father said. “He did football, soccer, baseball, track. But his favorite by far was football.” The last spring of his life, Fletcher’s flag football team won the championship. One of his best friends, MJ Roaldi, was the quarterback and Fletcher was the star receiver. Fletcher was fast, notably so. He once accidentally ran an entire 5k race in 24 minutes at eight years old. “In a lot of ways, he was my mini-me,” Jesse Merkel said. “Would have been a lot taller and probably more athletic than me.” Fletcher was competitive, too. At flag football games now, his friends feel his absence because there’s no one meticulously keeping score in their head like Fletcher did. “We were working on his ‘losing with grace’ skill,” Jesse said. In October 2024, that love of football inspired Mike Roaldi, MJ’s father, and Adam Dietenberger to take Fletcher and three of his friends – MJ, Sebi Dietenberger and Trip Sharpe – to a Golden Gophers game. They had little connection to the team, but when the Gophers upset the University of Southern California, the boys stormed the field along with the rest of the fans. “We suddenly got this picture of them on the field,” Jesse Merkel recalled. “He came home and he was just like, ‘You would never believe it! We were on the field and we’re with the players, and it was the coolest thing.’” It was Fletcher’s favorite day, his joy about the experience infectious. It was just like him to have such unbridled enthusiasm. For Fleck, it was “the only memory and moment that I had with Fletcher that I didn’t even know I had. You just never know who you’re impacting, and you never know how the universe and the world is going to pull you back together.” Ten months later, Fletcher was one of two students killed, along with 27 others who were injured, at the Annunciation Catholic School in Minneapolis, less than 10 miles from the University of Minnesota campus. The shooting took place while first through eighth graders were at Mass next to the school. Fletcher and 10-year-old Harper Moyski died next to their friends and classmates. “The day after the shooting, so the day after they lost him, I was at a park where we got together and comforted each other,” Mike Roaldi said. “There were four of Fletcher’s close friends there, and they were kind of playing tag, and then they would stop and talk. I overheard them at one point – 24 or 36 hours before Fletcher (had been) alive – and they just said something like, ‘Hey, you think he’s watching us right now?’ And then they started to talk about things that would be different without him, and it was clear how much he meant to them just in that conversation.” Fleck spoke publicly about the shooting after the Gophers’ next game. He had already told his players that football should be the smallest thing on their minds. They should dedicate their thoughts to the community that was impacted. “These are our kids,” he said, choking back tears at the podium. At Fletcher’s funeral, Will Sharpe, Trip’s father who had coached Fletcher in flag football, gave the eulogy. He talked about Fletcher’s love of life and sports and football and the time he and his friends found themselves on the field after Minnesota’s dramatic victory. Someone from the Gophers heard that and reached out to Sharpe through Facebook. Somebody gave Fleck the picture of Fletcher and his friends reveling in the uncomplicated joy that sports can offer a kid. The picture still sits on his desk. Just knowing he had helped make a happy memory for someone who wouldn’t get nearly enough of them: “That changes your life,” Fleck said. Waves of pain and moments of escape The first time the Annunciation community went to a Gopher game as honored guests was a couple months after the shooting. By then, the team had already sent more than 30 players to the school’s Fall Festival, where they spent hours playing wiffle ball with the students who were changed forever by two-and-a-half minutes of merciless violence. Jesse Merkel was not looking forward to the game. It still hurt, badly, to be around Fletcher’s friends. It felt senseless and unfair. Why did it have to be his son who was gone forever? Those thoughts made him feel guilty on top of the grief. But that day proved to be different. The Gophers invited Fletcher’s brother and three friends – Trip, MJ and Sebi – along with the fathers to be part of their game week. They attended practice, watched Fleck give his pregame speech and sat in club seats where they included a ticket for Fletcher. Somewhere along the way, Merkel and Fleck met for the first time. “He told me that he lost a son himself and that immediately, for better or worse, lets me put my guard down,” Jesse Merkel said. Colton Fleck died shortly after birth of a heart condition. His father is careful not to equate that loss to what the Fletchers and Moyskis are going through. “Pain comes to us in a lot of different ways and a lot of different-sized waves,” Fleck said, “and I can’t imagine the tidal wave that those families are experiencing.” But his son’s ashes are in an urn and he still chokes up talking about it. “I know what it’s like when people say things to you and you’re like, ‘Yeah, but you have no idea,’” Fleck said. “And then they go about their day and you still don’t have your child. “ It allowed Jesse Merkel to trust the intentions behind what Fleck had to say, but it also allowed them to be quiet together and just hold each other. Fleck gave Merkel a charm with a saint on it. “This is what I use to think about my son,” Fleck told him, “and I’d like you to have one.” The specificity and intimacy caught Merkel off guard. This wasn’t perfunctory or performative. The public persona of Fleck – someone quick with an inspirational quote – that had once rubbed him the wrong way, was not a persona at all. “That, for sure, stuck with me,” Merkel said. “I think that maybe the best word to describe PJ Fleck would be ‘genuine’ because what you see is what you get. Like it or not, it’s what you’re getting. And, when you’re able to get enough people with the right mindset together, I think that you can really do great things.” As they had the year before when Fletcher was in the stands, the Gophers won that game in dramatic fashion – an overtime win after which, once again, the crowd stormed the field. This time, Fletcher wasn’t among them, but his friends and family were. Defensive end Anthony Smith ran over to greet the group; then Fleck did as well, and finally the quarterback Drake Lindsey. Later, in the locker room, while wearing a Team Fletcher wristband, Fleck gave the boys each a game ball. He hugged Jesse Merkel, who closed his eyes and didn’t let go for several seconds. As MJ’s dad, Mike Roaldi, teared up, one of the players put his arm around the older man. Then the team hoisted the four boys onto their shoulders, bouncing them into the air as they chanted the school’s fight song. “When we came here, it was the first time that I was around them, and I was able to feed off of their joy and be happy for them,” Merkel said of seeing Fletcher’s friends relishing the experience. But that solace was bittersweet. “He would have loved it the most.” Gophers culture That was November 1, 2025. When he addressed the team in the locker room after the game, Fleck called the Annunciation community “family to us.” “And they will always be family to us,” he said at the time, “from now [to] forever.” And then, to very little fanfare, the Gophers made good on that sentiment. They invited Fletcher’s whole class out to a practice before last year’s bowl game. Players attended a Fishing for Fletcher fundraiser for the school. This fall, they had Fletcher’s friends and family back out for another game and then a practice during the bye week. For a costume event at school, Trip dressed as PJ Fleck. “I’m shocked. There is no obligation. There’s really no connection to Annunciation, or (from) my family to the U of M, and they just continue to show up. They have been a pillar of strength and joy,” Merkel said. “And they’ll be here as long as we want them to be here. I truly believe that.” Most sports teams at college and professional levels engage in charity; all purport to have a meaningful connection to the community that cheers for them. But what exists between the Gopher football team and a small group of families affected by the Annunciation Catholic school shooting goes beyond philanthropy. It’s a relationship. It’s one that is not entered into lightly. Because as difficult as it was for Fleck, himself a father intimately acquainted with loss, to embrace the grief of the situation head on, he’s asking his young players to do so as well. “He tells you that (when he recruits in) high school. Like, ‘Hey, you’re going to have to learn how to serve and give to people who can’t give anything to you,’” said Maverick Baranowski, a fifth-year linebacker. “If you don’t want to do that, you’re just not in the right place.” And then it continues – relentlessly, as is Fleck’s style – once players become part of the program. “This is why I’ve stayed here for five years – because of the people on the football team and on the staff,” Smith, the star defensive tackle said. “I think that’s the most attractive thing when it comes to this program as a whole, like, it teaches you how to be a man before you become a football player” That education is intentional. Fleck sees his role as taking teenagers and turning them into future fathers and partners. If that sounds trite, consider that college sports are increasingly transient and transactional in a world of transfer portals and NIL agreements. The Gophers’ commitment to prioritizing a perspective bigger than football isn’t some secret sauce to success – they’re solidly middle-of-the-pack in the Big Ten this season. It’s just who they really are. Merkel, and the other dads, seem amazed at the Gophers’ willingness and ability to continue to make themselves available for support. But Fleck said the reason for that, the key to embodying genuine empathy as a football team or a larger-than-life coach, is simple. “You can hold other people’s pain, you can hold other people’s experiences, because you choose to do it,” he said. For the young boys who had their childhoods shattered, and for the father whose son will never grow up, the relationship has provided a powerful counterbalance to the devastating revelation that life can be unimaginably cruel. “I have come to understand, after Fletcher was killed, that there is so much more good in the world than I thought before,” Jesse Merkel said. “But the bad is really bad.”

articles.title: The Fans Need a Break From WWE's Cody Rhodes
articles.summary: Over the years, many of the criticisms thrown at names like prime John Cena or Roman Reigns apply to a certain other name:
articles.body:
Over the years, many of the criticisms thrown at names like prime John Cena or Roman Reigns apply to a certain other name:

For whatever reason, Rhodes doesn't get the same heat, though. Maybe it's the name. Maybe it's the goodwill garnered by dramatically boosting the sport and options for wrestlers in the industry with AEW. Maybe he's just plucky and likable (sans the neck tattoo thing).

The Roman Reigns Curse Is Crushing WWE ☠️

The Bloodline's Status Heading Into WWE Survivor Series WarGames🩸

Regardless of the reason, Rhodes needs a break. And the fans need a break from Rhodes.

Zoom out. We're not that far removed from serious, justifiable outrage over WWE throwing Pat McAfee and a host of other garbage around the Rhodes-Randy Orton WrestleMania feud. It was a program that should've been for the ages, a true pro wrestling main event that looped in decades of history, story beats and character developments.

But Rhodes and Orton just got that chance in recent weeks, leading up to the payoff at Crown Jewel.

Maybe that's a tad harsh. But it didn't do much, either. One could argue, minus a three-second eye-roller of a thing with Tiffany Stratton, that it was the worst thing on the entire card.

Worst, because fans expected more. But it wound up as just more of the same. Same old spots, same old pacing, same old wishy-washy face-heel stuff.

The outrage over the meddling and crap around the 'Mania program was justified. But if this had been the payoff anyway, it would've just been another match on the two-night card at best, or a legacy-smudging event at worst.

That's a major indictment on Orton at this stage of his career, no doubt. But it's a really nice summation of Rhodes as a whole frankly, one could argue, since his AEW days.

There have been a lot of stagnant, skippable periods of Rhodes' WWE journey since his return. The slog to actually winning it all on the "journey" and then the Cena-lite title run were mired with little odd things, like winning tag titles with Jey Uso. Endless teases of heel turns that aren't actually heel turns, but just a really angry good guy who is conflicted.

Oversaturation is the word. Now, Rhodes is on the Hollywood screen with the Street Fighter movie (probably a fun popcorn flick, but the 6.1 IMDB rating is pretty fitting for Rhodes), he has his podcast for whatever reason and all the other random stuff. All this, while not even holding a title. If one were to flick on any screen right now, odds are one would see Rhodes before any other pro wrestler.

It's just too much. And it's been too much for a long time. The worst part? The air of stubbornness around Rhodes' unwillingness to go heel will remain, even upon his return after a hiatus. If he goes away for a while, only to come back with the same old character, the hype will fade almost instantly.

The heel turn isn't hard to pull off, either. Fans could yearn for a "Homelander Cody" sort of thing. But "Corporate Cody" might be even better. A nepo-like businessman who is a stand-in for the shareholders and always bringing up his friends at TKO and the ratings and all that stuff would be meta in a great way. Not "cool heel" either that makes some fans cheer for him, either.

In a way, Rhodes is a really good example of the modern pro wrestler. Gimmicks and changes used to matter much more. Rhodes is just the pro wrestler who wants to be really good and beat you because that's what they do, man. Tack on a splash of family references, sure, but there's not much of a character otherwise. Slapping a skull on the entrance graphics and a random mask above the USA-vibed attire and blonde hair does not a character make. Even Cena has jorts and jerseys and a theme. Rhodes borders on a randomizer found on a create-a-wrestler-feature at times.

What stings is the greatness everyone knows Rhodes is capable of at any point. But that's not going to be magically achieved in one week. There's no having the cake and eating it too for him. There's no going heel but staying with all the kayfabe-breaking media circus. Maybe that's the issue for him.

Said greatness won't pop up until the audience gets a break from Rhodes. Capitalizing on the good graces of the return wave after an absence with a refreshed approach is a must.

But if history tells us anything, Rhodes is more than content to stay the same, especially while the fanbase gives him a pass for the things it dings other Superstars for weekly.

articles.title: Spain vs England: UEFA Nations League – predictions, how to watch, teams
articles.summary: Spain, who are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive meetings, host England in Madrid on Sunday.
articles.body:
Who : Spain vs England What : UEFA Nations League, Group A3 Where : Metropolitano Stadium, Madrid, Spain When : Sunday, November 15, at 7:45pm (19:45 GMT). How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:45 GMT before our live text commentary stream.

England have the chance to avenge their defeat and end Spain’s 43-match unbeaten record when they face the reigning world champions in Sunday’s final Nations League group encounter.

Spain staged a 3-2 comeback victory at London’s Wembley Stadium in late September, as Lamine Yamal scored an early opener and Mikel Oyarzabal finished the job.

Spain and England have both sealed their berth in the competition’s quaterfinals, with La Roja assured of the top spot should they avoid defeat on Sunday. England, meanwhile, will finish second if they fail to beat the two-time World Cup winners.

Teenage sensation Yamal, with four goals, and Mikel Merino, with three, have headlined Spain’s attacking charge, while newly-crowned Ballon d’Or recipient Harry Kane leads England.

Before Spain vs England, here’s everything you need to know:

How have Spain played in the Nations League?

Spain have a perfect record and lead Group A3 with 15 points.

They beat England 3-2 in the first game, an away trip, and followed it with a 4-1 rout of Croatia at home.

Then, they beat Czechia 3-1 at home, followed by a 2-1 away win over Croatia and a 2-0 away win over Czechia.

How have England played in the Nations League?

England are second in Group A3 with 12 points from five games, having won four times and lost once.

Their Nations League campaign started with a 3-2 home defeat to Spain before Thomas Tuchel’s side beat Czechia 2-0 and thrashed Croatia 7-0 in back-to-back away fixtures.

Later, they beat Czechia 3-0 at home and Croatia 2-1.

Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run

Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid.

While victory offers little more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarterfinal in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat.

“It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said Tuchel.

“I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday.

“I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept,” the German added.

“It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.”

De la Fuente said their unbeaten record provided his players with extra motivation.

“We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” he explained.

“None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.”

What happened the last time Spain and England met?

Spain came from behind to beat England 3-2 in an entertaining Nations League encounter on September 26, denying the hosts a cathartic win after their painful World Cup exit.

Yamal put Spain ahead in the second minute, but Anthony Gordon equalised, and Kane added another as England ended the first half with a 2-1 lead.

The Three Lions captain missed a penalty in the second half, though, allowing Spain to bounce back, as Alex Baena found the equaliser before Oyarzabal sealed victory in the 74th minute.

Opta’s supercomputer favours Spain for victory. They have a 59.6 percent probability of winning, while England’s odds of victory are 19.3 percent.

There is a 21.1 percent chance the game ends in a draw.

Yamal is expected to face England after missing the last game with a knee problem. Nico Williams and Aymeric Laporte are doubtful

Probable Spain XI: Unai Simon; Marc Pubill, Pau Cubarsi, Dean Huijsen, Marc Cucurella; Dani Olmo, Rodri, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Mikel Oyarzabal, Alex Baena

Myles Lewis-Skelly returns from his suspension, while Ezri Konsa is also expected to return after missing the last game due to a knee injury.

Djed Spence (muscle) is doubtful, and Marc Guehi (muscle) remains out with injury.

Probable England XI: Jordan Pickford; Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall; Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice; Morgan Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon; Harry Kane

articles.title: El Fraga doblega a un peleón Voltregà y buscará la primera Copa Continental ante el Benfica
articles.standfirst: El vigente campeón de Europa se impuso por 4-0 para meterse en la final
articles.summary: El vigente campeón de Europa se impuso por 4-0
articles.body: El Esneca Fraga doblegó este sábado a un combativo Voltregà Movento Stern (4-0), que aguantó en el partido hasta que la argentina Adriana Soto rompió la resistencia catalana con el 2-0 a nueve minutos del final de la primera semifinal, disputada en el pabellón Joan Ortoll de Calafell. El vigente campeón de Europa buscará este domingo, en la final prevista para las 13:00 horas, el título de la primera edición femenina de la Copa Continental. Su rival será Benfica que venció al Sanjoanense por 4-2. Será la reedición de la última final de la Liga de Campeones, en la que el Fraga conquistó el segundo título continental de su historia tras imponerse por 4-1 en Coimbra (Portugal). El Fraga salió decidido a llevar la iniciativa y encontró pronto el premio. En el minuto 4, Carla Fontdegloria cazó un rechace dentro del área para abrir el marcador (1-0). Sin embargo, el Voltregà no se arrugó, plantó cara a su rival y resistió las acometidas aragonesas para mantener intactas sus opciones durante buena parte del encuentro. De hecho, el marcador no volvió a moverse hasta que, a nueve minutos del final, Adriana Soto encontró la manera de ampliar la ventaja y encarrilar el triunfo aragonés. Con el cuadro catalán obligado a arriesgar, el equipo que dirige Jordi Capdevila aprovechó los espacios para sentenciar el encuentro. La también argentina Julieta Fernández, de falta directa, y la española María Sanjurjo redondearon el 4-0 definitivo. 4 - Esneca Fraga: Ferrer; Arxé, Soto (1), Fontdegloria (1), Sanjurjo (1), -cinco inicial-, Payá, Fernández (1), Costa, Rubio e Iglesias (p.s). 0 - Voltregà Movento Stern: Sala, Anna Bosh, Vilamala, Vistos, Comas, -cinco inicial-, Canal, Fabrego, Ferran, Alexia Bosh y Masnou (p.s). articles.title: College football legend Brian Bosworth says he supports the controversial 24-team expanded playoff
articles.summary: College Football great Brian Bosworth said he likes the new College Football Playoff format as it gives more programs an opportunity to showcase themselves.
articles.body: College football legend Brian Bosworth is a fan of the controversially expanded playoff format. The 24-team format will begin in the 2027–28 season and run for five seasons, but fans don’t like it because it dilutes the impact of the regular season. However, Bosworth likes the new format because it gives more programs opportunities to compete on bigger stages. "It just gets bigger and better, and it deserves to be bigger and better because there's so many college programs that deserve the opportunity to show who they are," Bosworth told OutKick in a recent interview. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The Oklahoma football legend talked about the incredible parity in college football and how top teams lose nearly every weekend . Bosworth also said the expanded playoff gives more fans a reason to stay invested later into the season. "To expand to include colleges that otherwise would be forgotten. They're on the edge and you say, ‘Oh, maybe next year, maybe next year.’ It gives the fans some more hope. It gives them a dream. It gives them a destination and it keeps their passion alive," Bosworth said. When asked whether 24 teams realistically have a chance to win the national championship each season, Bosworth said not to discount the longshots. "There could be 10 or 12 really good teams, but there could be another 10 teams behind them that are just hungry and want an opportunity. So, yeah, it extends the season and it gives more teams an opportunity, but there's something to be said about the long shot or the hungry dog," Bosworth said. RAVENS STAR KYLE HAMILTON SAYS HE HATES WHERE COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS GOING AMID 24-TEAM PLAYOFF, NIL CHAOS The Wild West of the NIL Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is returning to the Bulldogs next season on a $7.5 million deal that could reach $9 million with incentives, according to multiple reports. Bosworth has said the exorbitant amounts of money involved in some of these contracts are a "head-scratcher." "The money has gotten to a point where it's just a head scratcher. I'm a firm believer of putting some fences around it and controlling the fact that not every school is going to have the deep pockets in which to go deep into," Bosworth said. "I think the fairness of it should be across the board that every team has the same pool so that they can manage the team across the board. Everybody's doing the same thing on the same page and you don't have somebody that's funneling money into it and then you can have these crazy contracts the way they're going about it now." Bosworth noted that Taylor is an amazing player, but football isn’t a one-man show. If the team doesn’t invest in the players around him, it will struggle to play well. "But it's not a one-man show (because) great quarterbacks can fail based upon their offensive scheme, the play calling, the injuries on the offensive line. If you've got a defense that's super porous, you know. It really does take a team to be an elite team to get into the conversation to be a championship in the conference and then maybe get to the playoffs," Bosworth said. Bosworth knows what it takes to have a winning team, as he won the 1985 national championship and three Big Eight titles. He won the Butkus Award as the nation’s top linebacker in both 1985 and 1986. articles.title: Matvei Michkov, Simon Edvinsson and the Young NHL Players Who Need a Trade
articles.summary: Can you consciously uncouple as a hockey team and prospect or young player? Because there are a lot of them who need to.
articles.body:
Can you consciously uncouple as a hockey team and prospect or young player? Because there are a lot of them who need to.

If it isn't breakup season for these four young NHL players and their organizations, it should be.

Sitting down to research this piece proved fascinating; quite a few of our targets from recent years, or obvious targets that we haven't addressed, have been traded before the 2026-27 season started. Simon Nemec moved from the New Jersey Devils to the Calgary Flames, Mason McTavish got shipped off from the Anaheim Ducks to the St. Louis Blues, and the Ducks also sent Olen Zellweger to the Buffalo Sabres.

Because this is the NHL, however, and teams would so often rather swap young players out with shiny new toys than invest in their development, we've still got plenty to look at.

We've all heard the cliché "second verse, same as the first"; the situation we're seeing with Matvei Michkov and the Philadelphia Flyers is more like "one millionth verse, same as the first".

Stop me if you've heard this before: a dynamic young forward, often from Russia or Sweden, or somewhere else overseas, who is drafted for his flashy offensive talent, and then once he actually gets to the NHL, he's labeled cocky and lazy, and called out for not wanting to play defense or be a team player.

It's happened so many times you could set your watch by it.

Not every situation fits the mold exactly, but there are enough repeated elements that the stereotype is known for a reason. Michkov is just another in a long line. The problem is that the Flyers are rebuilding, and they need him — not some hypothetical version of him that is always defensively responsible or constantly passing to teammates instead of shooting, but the full, unleashed version, in top form, as a key part of their attempts to claw out of this pit they've fallen into.

Did we mention he's leading the Flyers in goals?

Michkov's ice time fluctuates; there are alleged off-ice issues between him and teammates; he was a healthy scratch during the playoffs last year; and he's coming up on restricted free agency. The Flyers are going to have to make a decision sooner rather than later on whether to embrace Michkov as he is, or utilize him to acquire more pieces for their rebuild while his trade value is high, before things sour to the point of desperation (see: any number of trades we've seen recently).

Unlike Michkov, Simon Edvinsson has requested a trade. The highly skilled, highly valued Detroit Red Wings defenseman and restricted free agent has not played a game for the team this season, choosing to sit out instead of signing a new contract.

To paraphrase The Suite Life of Zack and Cody: How do you lose a talented young defenseman? You forget to cherish him.

Or, in this case, you don't build a competitive team around him, and your contract offers aren't enticing enough to make up for that. And because he's a restricted free agent without arbitration eligibility, the only tool left at his disposal, per the NHL and NHLPA's collective bargaining agreement, is to sit out until he gets at least part of what he wants.

RFAs of Edvinsson's class really have no mechanisms of control in the situation he is in other than refusing to play, and it's something that gets a lot of mixed reactions. The word selfish gets thrown around a lot; guys get labeled as "not team players", only in it for the money, et cetera. That can sour a relationship between player and fanbase as much as it can player and front office, or player and team. Eventually, you reach a point of no return, and a trade really is the best solution for everyone involved.

Obviously, this is a nightmare for the Red Wings front office, which is already trying to facilitate a Larkin trade, and—sorry, Red Wings fans—we've got another player from that team on this list too.

Here's the trick: Edvinsson has to sign before Dec. 1 if he wants to play this season, with anyone . Not just the Red Wings. Tick-tock, Shawn Horcoff and co.

Sorry Red Wings fans, but we've hit another iceberg.

Nate Danielson has two points in 13 NHL games this season and three points in one AHL game this season. It's a discrepancy that's common in young players, and it's one that can stem from a multitude of causes; it doesn't mean that he isn't capable of being effective at the NHL level. In Danielson's case, he's averaging around 10-11 minutes per night playing on the fourth line, on a team that frankly is not good. That's going to make it difficult for almost anyone to gain traction on a long-term basis.

Danielson's style is agile, with effective handling and good skating. His playmaking could use improvement, for certain, but that's not something he is going to get playing only 10 or 11 minutes per night. Prior to his professional career, he was often called out for succeeding at rush offense; he continues to be attentive to detail and effective in the subtle, small areas of the game.

While junior players often have to switch up parts of their playing style to be effective at the professional level, there's a pretty big difference between realizing that the areas in which you were a successful distributor or offense-creator are not going to work the same way they did in juniors and being shoved down to an inconsistent fourth-line role.

Development is a process, and Danielson's is not one that the Red Wings have invested in. It may not be a bad idea to explore swapping him out for someone else as a way to kickstart the trade dominoes falling and give everyone a fresh beginning.

The writing is on the wall with this one. The Chicago Blackhawks don't trust defenseman Kevin Korchinski, but they're also not playing him in any way that gives him the opportunity to change that or earn that trust back. What is a guy supposed to do here?

Korchinski is, believe it or not, still only 22 years old. He's played 5 games this season. Since his first NHL season, his opportunities have dwindled in both games played and time on ice, and now he can't even be sent down to the Rockford IceHogs to get playing time there because he would have to go on waivers, and the Blackhawks don't want to lose him and get nothing in return.

Have you noticed yet that they don't even seem to have a plan for what to do with this kid?

It's the age-old story of a young, dynamic defenseman who is not instantly a world-beater, so he must be a bust, so we're going to let everyone else pass him and not invest any time or effort into his development. Sink or swim on your own, buddy. He's very clearly sitting on the outside here, and it's time for the Blackhawks to cut their losses and let Korchinski out of limbo.

This is a team that, frankly, sucks right now—they've won a total of five of their nineteen games. Other defensemen have been allowed to make mistakes that Korchinski would be torched for because they play a lower-risk style of game; his ceiling is high, and he helps drive scoring chances, so more is expected of him, and so he gets punished more. He's far from the first young defenseman for this to happen to.

Obviously, he's not a perfect player, but in order to fix any warts in his game, he has to actually see the ice. Cut him loose and move on for the good of everyone.

articles.title: Nate Wiggins details how the Ravens' defense can limit Justin Herbert
articles.summary: Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins says the defense is focusing on discipline to stop Justin Herbert and the Chargers.
articles.body:
Limiting explosive plays has become a key focus for the Baltimore Ravens defense, particularly with another challenging quarterback on the schedule. As the team prepares for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers , cornerback Nate Wiggins says the focus is on improving recognition, staying disciplined, and making opponents work for every yard.

Head coach Jesse Minter has discussed the need to reduce the number of big plays Baltimore allows, and Wiggins explained that the defense is working to address the issue through better preparation and execution.

The cornerback said the team is spending time identifying offensive formations and understanding the keys within the defensive scheme.

"[We're] really just dialing in on all the formations and keys of the defense and making them throw the checkdowns and just tackle."

That approach will be especially important against Herbert, whose ability to push the ball downfield can put pressure on opposing secondaries. The Chargers quarterback has the arm strength to make difficult throws and the athleticism to create opportunities when plays break down.

Wiggins understands that Baltimore will need to be aware of those abilities throughout the game. The Ravens can't afford to lose discipline in coverage or give Herbert opportunities to take advantage of defensive mistakes.

"Yes, [Justin Herbert]'s arm talent, he's a great athlete. We have to be conscious of him throwing the deep ball, and I feel like we have the DBs to do that."

Wiggins' confidence in the secondary will be important as Baltimore looks to put together a more consistent defensive performance. The Ravens have talent in the defensive backfield, but execution will be critical against a quarterback capable of changing a game with one throw.

The emphasis on limiting explosive plays also goes beyond simply preventing deep passes. Baltimore will need to tackle effectively, keep plays in front of the defense, and avoid allowing shorter completions to turn into significant gains.

With Herbert and the Chargers coming to town, the Ravens will have an opportunity to demonstrate whether their renewed focus can translate into better results on the field.

articles.title: Oklahoma AD rips 'wrong outcome' in moving Ole Miss game to Sunday
articles.summary: The FAA ground stop forced the Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma game to Sunday, and the Sooners AD isn't happy about it.
articles.body:
The FAA ground stop on Friday sent the sports world into some chaos, with some teams having to scramble and eight college football contests getting their start times moved .

The most extreme of those changes? Ole Miss will play Oklahoma on Sunday instead of Saturday at 1 p.m. And the decision by SEC commissioner Greg Sankey didn't sit well with Sooners athletic director Roger Denny.

In a strongly worded statement posted on Saturday morning, he had a lot to say, noting how tough the decision was under the "extraordinary circumstances," but he also didn't think it was fair and that there was a threat of a forfeit if the Sooners didn't play on Sunday.

"Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans. Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. ... "I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation. We've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play this game when directed, but we remained steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening."

articles.title: Sheila Ford Hamp Goes Viral for Epic Moment in Germany
articles.summary: Detroit Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp tapped a keg at Munich's Hofbräuhaus, surrounded by Lions fans ahead of Sunday's Patriots game.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp is getting into the spirit of Germany, and she appears to be having an absolute blast doing it.

With the Lions preparing to take on the New England Patriots on Sunday, Hamp made a special appearance at the famous Hofbräuhaus in Munich, where she tapped a keg in front of a large gathering of Lions fans and members of the Ford family.

As you can see in the video posted by Justin Rogers, Hamp was surrounded by cheering supporters as she took part in the traditional German celebration.

The Hofbräuhaus has been transformed into the official Detroit Lions fan pub for the team's trip to Germany. Fans have been gathering throughout the week to celebrate the franchise's return to international football.

Hamp isn't the only recognizable Lions figure to get involved in the festivities. Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders also tapped a keg at the historic beer hall on Thursday, with fellow Lions legend Calvin Johnson joining the celebration.

The atmosphere in Munich has been electric, with Detroit supporters making their presence felt thousands of miles from Ford Field. Now, Lions fans are hoping the celebration continues Sunday when Detroit faces New England at Allianz Arena.

Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX. And if Saturday's celebration is any indication, the Lions certainly won't be lacking support in Germany.
