articles.body:
Despite speculation connecting the Pittsburgh Steelers to New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson ahead of the NFL trade deadline, a new report suggests the team was never seriously involved.

According to ESPN's Rich Cimini, the Steelers were not among the teams pursuing Wilson. Instead, the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers were the two teams with reported interest in the Pro Bowl wide receiver.

Wilson has been a popular name in trade speculation given the Jets' ongoing struggles and questions surrounding the direction of the franchise. His talent and ability to serve as a legitimate No. 1 receiving option naturally made him an attractive potential target for contending teams.

For Pittsburgh, the reported lack of interest puts another potential trade target to rest. The Steelers have continued working to improve their receiving corps, but it appears Wilson was never part of their plans as the trade deadline approached.

articles.title: UConn women’s rough road continues at No. 7 Louisville: What to know, how to watch
articles.summary: A week ago, Geno Auriemma was worried, perhaps half joking, said that the UConn women’s basketball team could be looking at a four-game losing streak, unthin...
articles.body:
A week ago, Geno Auriemma was worried, perhaps half joking, said that the UConn women's basketball team could be looking at a four-game losing streak, unthinkable for a program that once went 30 years without a two-game losing streak.

But he had lined up a nonconference schedule that included four consecutive ranked teams, and when the Huskies started off with a double-digit loss at Michigan on Nov. 5, the unthinkable looked like a possibility. That has since been buried with a couple of signature, convincing UConn wins over Iowa at home and at Ohio State, so, no, they would not finish last in the Big Ten. In fact, the Huskies may be hitting their stride.

Now they have another road game against a top 10 team, at No. 7 Louisville, an old conference rival in the original Big East and a frequent nonconference opponent since.

Louisville, with its ACC schedule coming up, has started its season with five mid-major opponents and defeated them easily. Coach Jeff Walz took his team on the road to Ball State for a little tougher test in the last game, and the Cardinals won, 94-73. Their average margin of victory so far is 38.4 points.

"I think it's good for the game," Walz told reporters after . "More top 10 programs need to go on the road because a lot of our mid-majors that are really good can only play top 25 teams on the road. They won't come to their place and play. We need to be able to go on the road and play a place like this before we start up our conference play because you got to figure out a way to win on the road in the ACC."

Louisville was second to Duke in the ACC preseason coaches' poll. The Huskies will play Duke in Boston on Nov. 28, so before long they will know how they would stack up in that power conference. They have still another Big Ten opponent coming up with Maryland in December.

"My goal was not to finish last in the Big Ten," Auriemma said. "A schedule like this can be really harmful to your team if it doesn't go well. It doesn't necessarily give you a chance to play a lot of players because you're trying to win the game. But it gives you a chance to go to practice the next day and 'I'd rather know now rather than in January what we are, what we've got, who we can count on."

In UConn's loss to Michigan, Auriemma felt players were "standing around" expecting Sarah Strong and Jovana Popovic to carry the team. In the games since, the Huskies have gotten more from the supporting cast, with Blanca Quinonez scoring 21 vs. Iowa, Ashlynn Shade scoring 15 at Ohio State. Sophomore Kelis Fisher scored nine points in only five minutes on Thursday.

"We scored 87 points and Blanca didn't score and Pop was 1-for-7, so we had enough people step up that we were up three at halftime. That was huge. (The supporting cast) really found themselves a little bit. That's all we need from them. When it's your turn, you're at Connecticut, so you're expected to do it."

Strong has taken charge on a different level in these last two games, scoring 64 points.

Freshman Olivia Vukosa, who had 12 rebounds against Ohio State, has generally not looked overmatched against the high level of competition and could be in line for more minutes.

"Liv had a great game," Auriemma told reporters at Ohio State. "She had the best game of her young college career. She took a big step in the direction that we want her to go. And I hope that we can prepare her to have more of these games."

UConn and Louisville have met 24 times, in regular season conference and nonconference games, conference tournaments and NCAA Tournament games as deep as the Final Four. Here's what you need to know about the game:

What to know: No. 4 UConn at No. 7 Louisville

Site: Venue: KFC Yum! Center, Louisville

History: UConn leads the series, 21-3. In their last meeting, UConn prevailed, 79-66, at Louisville on Nov. 4, 2025.

TV/stream: ESPN (announcers Mike Monaco, Andraya Carter).

Radio: UConn Sports Network from Learfield (Fox Sports 97-9 FM, WGCH 1490 AM, WAVX 1300 AM, WICH 1310 AM, WILI 1400 AM). Announcers: Bob Joyce, Debbie Fiske.

What to expect from Louisville: The Cardinals have four starters scoring in double digits, including Tajianna Robers (16.4), Imari Berry (15.2), Zamareya Jones (10.2) and amd Amiya Joyner (10.0), so they have balance among starters. This will be Louisville's first high-major opponent, so it will be the first big test for the Cardinals.

articles.title: Luke Weaver Reflects on Trade to Pirates
articles.summary: Luke Weaver talks about what it was like being traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates were more aggressive in mid-season roster additions than they typically were during the 2026 season.

For the first time in a long time, Pittsburgh's front office was a buyer instead of a seller at the deadline. One of the team's big moves was adding relief pitcher Luke Weaver from the New York Mets.

Weaver's trade to Pittsburgh wasn't the first time he moved from one big-league team to another. In fact, it was the third time during the pitcher's career that he had been traded.

Weaver said that this part of the job is never easy, given how much moving to a new city can impact a family as a whole. He said that sometimes the baseball side of things "becomes an afterthought."

That said, this mid-season transition didn't take away from Weaver's impressions of the Pirates team in 2026 and what their potential could be moving forward.

Weaver is only 33 years old. In that grand scheme of things, that's not old whatsoever. However, on the Pirates roster, he is certainly one of the veterans and easily one of the most experienced players.

Still, one of the main takeaways that Weaver had during his short time in Pittsburgh to close out the season was just how exciting the Pirates' future is. The young core the team has is real, and Weaver believes that group will only get better over the years.

"It's a young core. There's a lot of studs. I mean, it's unbelievable," said Weaver.

"I'm like, I feel like the old guy, which is crazy, but I feel like I'm not physically at the old part because I'm trying to keep up with them."

Weaver talked about how one of the biggest transitions for him after being traded to Pittsburgh, or any new organization, for that matter, is working with an entirely different catcher staff.

It takes time to build those relationships, and everything moves faster when you join a new team in the middle of the year.

"There could be some hoops to jump through," Weaver explained.

"You sit down there for the 1st 20 minutes you're there and you're like, this is where I like you to set up. This is what I like to do. This is how I think."

Weaver's first two-month stint with the Pirates was an interesting one. Pittsburgh was clearly viewed as the team's closer after the trade, but the team didn't have many save opportunities immediately after the deadline. This inconsistency on the mound was certainly reflected in Weaver's stats .

The right-hander appeared in 18 games with the Pirates and posted a 4.96 ERA and a 1.35 WHIP. The numbers could have been worse, but they still weren't exactly what Pittsburgh was hoping for.

Even though Weaver's stats weren't exactly what the team was envisioning, the veteran pitcher will still be a key piece to the team's success in 2027, and it appears that he's bought into what the Pirates are building.

articles.title: 49ers Announce Keenan Allen Decision Ahead of Cowboys Game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in what head coach Kyle Shanahan called the biggest game of the year. San Francisco is 7-1 and sitt...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in what head coach Kyle Shanahan called the biggest game of the year. San Francisco is 7-1 and sitting atop the NFC. Dallas is fighting to stay in the mix after a disappointing start.

The 49ers' receiver room has taken hits all season. Mike Evans is sidelined with Achilles tendinitis. The depth that carried San Francisco through the first two months has been tested repeatedly, and earlier this week the front office moved to address it.

On Tuesday, the 49ers traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen. By Wednesday morning, Allen was already in the building. On Friday, Shanahan made his plans for Sunday official.

Allen will make his 49ers debut against Dallas.

The timeline from trade to game day moved fast. Allen was at the Colts facility on Tuesday morning when he learned he had been dealt. He packed a bag, flew west, and touched down in the Bay Area after midnight. He was at the facility before 6 AM for his physical.

Allen said the shift in environment hit him immediately.

"I get a little boost in the way I feel coming into the building," Allen said. "Just being a part of the guys, it's a hell of a locker room. Obviously, these guys have accomplished so much in the past years. I'm running on just pure energy right now."

The veteran nearly signed with the 49ers as a free agent before choosing Indianapolis in the offseason. He caught 40 passes for 351 yards with a touchdown across eight games for Indianapolis before the trade brought him to where he almost landed months earlier.

Allen owns 1,095 career receptions, the most among active NFL wide receivers. His career receiving yardage and touchdown totals place him among the top five active players in both categories. The resume is extensive.

Brock Purdy has already seen the football IQ show up in practice.

"I feel like he understands our plays and our formations, and he's been around the block and understands what the routes are and where he needs to be," Purdy said. "I really do think he's got a good grasp on what we're doing this week."

Allen acknowledged the terminology is different from what he ran in Indianapolis, but said the concepts are familiar. When asked what he expects on Sunday, his answer was simple.

In an unusual twist in the schedule, Sunday's game against Dallas will be the second straight week Allen faces the Cowboys. He hauled in four receptions for 26 yards against Dallas in his final game as a Colt.

Allen went from a 2-7 team to the best record in the NFC overnight.

The 49ers needed receiver depth. Allen provides it immediately. Whether he can learn enough of the playbook in four days to make a significant impact against Dallas remains the question, but Purdy's early assessment suggests the transition is ahead of schedule.

Sunday will be the first real look at what the fit becomes on the field. Allen is ready. The 49ers are counting on it.

articles.title: Ex-Giants $19 Million Starter Emerges as Option for Division Rival
articles.summary: Prior to the NFL trade deadline, the New York Giants pursued several different running backs, including superstars Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor.This int...
articles.body:
Prior to the NFL trade deadline, the New York Giants pursued several different running backs, including superstars Derrick Henry and Jonathan Taylor.

This interest came despite running back Cam Skattebo coming off the best performance of his career one week before the deadline. However, despite Skattebo's hot stretch recently, that does not mean the Giants had certainty all season at the running back position.

In fact, Skattebo even felt he was being punished earlier in the season, which led to New York starting veteran running back Najee Harris. After Harris started New York's game against the New Orleans Saints, the veteran complained about not being able to get into a rhythm due to a low number of carries. A few days later, Harris was released by the Giants.

After the trade deadline has come and gone, Harris has now been viewed as a fit for the NFC East division rival Dallas Cowboys.

Former New York Giants Starting Running Back Seen as Fit for Dallas Cowboys

Following the NFL trade deadline, Bleacher Report's Moe Moton identified the best team fits for some of the top free agents available on the market.

Regarding former New York Giants running back Najee Harris, Moton wrote: "After eclipsing 1,000 rushing yards in four consecutive seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Najee Harris has struggled to find career stability on a second team.

On a one-year, $5.25 million contract, Harris appeared in only three games with the Los Angeles Chargers before tearing his Achilles tendon in September 2025.

This year, coming off an injury, Harris signed another single-term, prove-it deal with the New York Giants. They released him six weeks into the season after he publicly expressed dissatisfaction with his role. The 28-year-old running back has been a free agent since then.

Nonetheless, Harris could be an asset to a team that needs a short-yardage tailback. He's a 6'1″, 242-pound bruising ball-carrier who can pick up first downs in critical situations and close drives near the goal line"

Regarding how Harris could fit with the Cowboys, Moton added: "Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones expects backup running back Tyler Goodson to miss time with a knee injury. The Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to their practice squad, but he has a history of injuries. Harris could be a solid complement to Javonte Williams in the Cowboys' ground game."

Harris did not produce much with the New York Giants this season. In five games, Harris registered 31 carries for 99 rushing yards. His 3.2 yards per carry were the fewest of his career.

While the former first-round pick did have success with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Harris was never a particularly explosive runner. In his limited time with the Giants, the burst he once had felt even more diminished after his Achilles tear.

Harris has totaled over $19 million in career earnings after being a first-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft.

Among the reasons the Giants released Harris was that the team was carrying four running backs on the roster, which head coach John Harbaugh explained was hard. Unfortunately, Tyrone Tracy went on injured reserve one game after the Giants moved on from Harris.

articles.title: Ravens' Nate Wiggins eyes a fresh start after missing Jaguars game
articles.summary: Ravens cornerback Nate Wiggins returns from illness ready to help the defense against the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body:
Missing a game is never easy for a player who wants to be available for his teammates, and Nate Wiggins is especially eager to return after being sidelined by illness. Wiggins returned to the practice field after an illness kept him out against Jacksonville, giving the Ravens a key cornerback as they prepare to face Justin Herbert and the Chargers . Wiggins welcomed the opportunity to rejoin his teammates, while Baltimore's secondary faces the task of limiting downfield completions Monday night.

Wiggins has made it clear that being on the field is important to him. Whether it's helping the defense execute its assignments or competing against some of the league's top receivers, he wants to be part of the action. Speaking with reporters ahead of the Chargers game, Wiggins expressed his excitement about returning and continuing to build on his development.

"I'm happy to be back. Knowing myself, I don't like missing games. I like to be out there for the team. I'm happy to be back and show the world who Nate Wiggins is and just keep doing it."

His return comes as Baltimore looks to regroup following an inconsistent stretch. The extra time off gave the team a chance to get healthy, reconnect, and refocus before starting the next part of its schedule.

Wiggins believes the reset was important for the entire group and expects the Ravens to show a different level of energy moving forward.

"I just thank God for the reset we had. I feel like we needed a reset. Everybody [can now] get back together, [and] everybody will do what we do. I feel like in this game, we are going to show the world that the Ravens are back and we're ready to go."

The cornerback's return gives Baltimore another option in the secondary as the defense prepares for a challenging matchup against the Chargers. With the Ravens looking to improve their overall consistency, having their defensive backs available will be important.

Wiggins is ready to get back to work, and Monday night offers a chance to show what he can bring to the defense as the Ravens look to get back on track.

articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter gave an injury update on Lamar Jackson and his thumb injury. According to Minter, injuries like the one Jackson suffered and require surgery usually take 6-10 weeks to heal.

But as ESPN's Adam Schefter has reported, Jackson had already undergone thumb surgery last week . That means if Jackson meets the lower end of Minter's specified timeline, he would still be able to return later this season.

Jackson suffered the thumb injury in the very first snap of their 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 1. That was his first game back after missing a month due to a hamstring injury.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Ravens, who were 3-1 with Jackson as the starter in their first four games, have fallen off a cliff since, going 1-4 without him. His backup, Tyler Huntley, has gone down with a season-ending toe injury. Jacoby Brissett, whom they acquired from the Arizona Cardinals before the trade deadline, is set to make his first start for the team in Week 10 against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

At this point, it's unclear whether it would be worth it for the Ravens to bring Jackson back even if he were fully recovered from his thumb injury. It would depend largely on where the Ravens stand by then. They have a relatively easy schedule coming up as their next four games will be against the Chargers, Panthers, Texans and Buccaneers, who are all currently under .500.

If Brissett can keep them within playoff contention, perhaps it would be justifiable to bring Jackson back. But even then, it would take something special for Jackson and the Ravens to transform into serious title contenders given their struggles this season.

articles.title: Red-hot Franklin shuts down Whiteland in girls basketball
articles.summary: Ella McCrary scored 18 points as Franklin defeated Whiteland, 72-49.
articles.body:
WHITELAND − It was a hot and electric night for the Franklin girls basketball team in a 72-49 victory over Whiteland on Friday, Nov. 13.

After a slow start, Franklin junior guard Ella McCrary caught fire, burying four 3-pointers in the first quarter en route to scoring 18 on the night.

At the 4:47 mark, the Lady Cubs led, 10-0, with McCrary leading the way.

"I think the good encouragement from my teammates and them hyping me up when I made a shot really helped me continue to be hot," McCrary said.

In the span of 1 minute and 30 seconds, both the Warriors (2-2) and the Cubs (3-1) combined for five threes, trading buckets.

"Our game plans [are] generally the same," Franklin coach Brian Klem said. "We try to take open shots and make easy passes … early, it seemed like they were threes, and then we got some twos later."

The hot streaks ended with 3:18 left in the first quarter and the Lady Cubs leading, 16-11.

Once the streak ended, so did the offense, the quarter ending on a huge block by Franklin's Addi King as Cubs took a 21-12 lead.

The second quarter started with a statement from one of Indiana's rising stars, freshman Abby Boner, who had two huge steals to lead Whiteland on a 12-0 run.

Boner finished with 9 points, well below her 19.0 average as Franklin forged a 34-29 halftime lead.

Then Franklin opened the third quarter scoring 11 straight points to extend its lead to 45-29, and senior Izzy Stillabower hit a huge three to push the lead to 50-33 with 3:16 left in the third quarter.

Although the third quarter ended with Whiteland trailing, 54-39, it came out firing on all cylinders in the fourth quarter. A minute in, junior Aurora Lightfoot drained a three to cut the lead to 12.

The Warriors then pressed full court, f orcing a turnover and turning it into a quick layup to cut their deficit to 54-44 and forcing Klem to call a timeout.

"We're just working on staying consistent throughout the game [and] we're just trying to put a whole game together with consistent effort," Klem said. "And I think for the most part, we did it; we had a few lapses where they came back on us a little bit, but I'm happy overall with it."

Fortunately for Klem, King took over, scoring 7 points in the last three minutes of the game.

"I definitely wanted to look for my shot, but getting my teammates open and getting the ball up the court was my goal," King said.

Three-pointers from Stillabower and junior Aleah Singleton put Franklin up, 63-46.

The two teams will play Nov. 17 in the Johnson County Tournament.

"We play them again on Tuesday, so we wanted to show them that they got something to worry about on Tuesday and that we're coming out with great intensity, great defense and we're not letting them win this game," McCrary said.

articles.title: Ravens' Derrick Henry sets a clear standard for second-half turnaround
articles.summary: Derrick Henry urges Ravens fans to look ahead as the team aims to reset and improve during the second half.
articles.body:
Despite a challenging first half of the season, Derrick Henry believes Baltimore has an opportunity to turn things around. With the team coming off an extended break and Lamar Jackson working toward a return, the veteran running back is focused on helping his teammates reset, regroup, and respond over the remaining weeks.

The Ravens have faced their share of adversity, and the results haven't consistently matched expectations. Henry understands that fans want to see improvement, but he believes the players remain committed to giving everything they have. During his media availability ahead of Monday night's game against the Chargers , Henry delivered a message to the Ravens Flock about the team's approach moving forward.

"We're going to go out there and give it 100% every time we step in this building and every time we step on the field. We know the results haven't been what they wanted it to be, but we've had some time off to get refreshed and ready to take on the challenge for this next half. Hopefully, we get them back and are ready to roll the way we need to."

The extended break provided Baltimore with an opportunity to recover from the physical demands of the season while also getting a mental reset. Henry believes that time away can be beneficial as the team prepares for the challenges ahead. He also emphasized that the Ravens can't afford to dwell on what has already happened. Instead, the focus needs to be on the present and approaching every week with the right mindset.

"I think it's a team message. We had some time to get away, refresh and get our bodies back under us, and also our mental. Now it is time to approach this and focus on being 1-0 each and every week. The past is the past. You can't change anything about that."

Henry believes the team needs to show what Ravens football looks like in all three phases, rather than allowing previous results to dictate its approach.

"But it's about the present and how you approach every day, so when we go out there, we have the right mindset. We put on display the way we want to put on display on how we want to play these games and play Ravens-style football in all three phases."

The running back also addressed the trade speculation that surrounded his name ahead of the deadline. Rather than getting caught up in the outside noise, Henry made it clear that his attention remains on Baltimore and the upcoming matchup.

"That's in the past. I'm here, and I'm focused on playing the Chargers. Whatever that was, it was. I'm a Raven."

For Henry, the message is simple: Baltimore has to turn the page. The Ravens have an opportunity to put together a stronger second half, but that starts with how they prepare and perform each week.

articles.title: OTB Staff Picks 2026: Rutgers vs Nebraska
articles.summary: Our writers predict Rutgers vs Nebraska.
articles.body:
After losing to Wisconsin 31-10 on the road last week, Rutgers football will return home to take on Nebraska this Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:30. The Scarlet Knights, 2-7, will face the 5-4 Cornhuskers, who are coming into this game after being beaten by Illinois 24-13. As is tradition here at OnTheBanks, the staff will try to guess the score of the game and give context as to why they think that way.

Rutgers will once again be the "get right game" for their opponent, even though Nebraska has been on a four-game losing streak. No Duff, no Lonergan, no Asamoah, and possibly no Surace means a long day for the Scarlet Knight offense. Coming into the season, we knew that the offense would have to be the driving force for Rutgers to win games, and it just can't do that against a good defense missing three of its four best offensive players. The defense likely won't be able to make up for what the offense now lacks because their improvement compared to last year has not been enough to give confidence that they can stop the Cornhuskers consistently.

With Rutgers overall firepower in the wide receiver and running back room, it's hard to imagine they will be shut out, but Nebraska's defense will not make it easy for the depleted offense. On the flip side, the Cornhuskers have the horses to wear down the Knights' defense, as we have seen in game after game. Like last game, Rutgers keeps it close in the first half before getting exposed in the second.

Rutgers is 1-4 at home this year; the one win is against Howard.

Greg Schiano is 26-42 in the month of November all time; he's 7-17 in Schiano 2.0 and he's already 0-1 this year. Three of those seven wins came in 2024 when the team went 3-1, beating Maryland, Illinois, and Michigan State.

KJ Duff is out. And, reading Andrew's notes: when did they say Lonergan out and Surace maybe ? I missed that! Sheesh!

But, the coach has a new lease on life, returning in 2027; so, that's off the table and no longer a distraction.

On the other side of the field, Nebraska is shaken from its recent fails, and Matt Ruhle is among the coaches on the hot seat . Pretty much as he's been all season. And he's moving up the list; he might be coaching for his job.

The Huskers hung tough before falling to Indiana; crazy side note: I was listening to the game on Sirius XM while I was doing work at home that day; they played well. Same thing happened against Oregon. They're a decent team but just not able to finish against better squads. Rutgers isn't that.

Please, someone tell me how we win this.

It's Military Appreciation Day in Piscataway, and to honor our military, Rutgers decided to wave the white flag by letting Greg stay another year.

Rutgers is going into battle short on supplies. No Duff, no Lonergan, no Asamoah, maybe no Surace, and still a question mark under center. That's a unit without its heavy artillery. Let's not try to win an air war. Make it trench warfare on this special day, and run the ball even when it's two yards a carry, take the clock with you, punt deep, and make Nebraska march the whole field every time.

Nebraska has lost four straight, and Matt Rhule might be coaching for his job. That's the kind of desperation that makes a team dangerous, not tight. The Huskers need this one more than Rutgers does, and they'll play like it.

The defense can hold the line for a while. Like we've seen all season, they'll keep it close into the second half, but you can only defend a position for so long without reinforcements. Eventually an offense that can't stay on the field wears the defense out, and Nebraska breaks through.

Greg Schiano is returning in 2027. Does that do anything to help the Scarlet Knights find a spark? The answer is no.

It is hard to accomplish this without the presence of KJ Duff, the lack of a run game, and major questions under center no matter who of the three are starting.

Nebraska has played competitively this year, especially against superior opponents. This feels like a game to show out a little bit. There is not much to say from here on out for Rutgers.

articles.title: Clippers end brutal losing streak vs. Thunder with stunning late surge as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander falls short
articles.summary: Darius Garland made a three-point play with 50.4 seconds left to lift the Los Angeles Clippers past the Oklahoma City Thunder, 113-122, in the NBA Cup at In...
articles.body:
Darius Garland made a three-point play with 50.4 seconds left to lift the Los Angeles Clippers past the Oklahoma City Thunder, 113-122, in the NBA Cup at Intuit Dome on Friday.

Garland's clutch play capped off the Clippers' 7-0 closing run. They survived the 40-point performance of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who missed his last-gasp attempt, allowing Los Angeles to escape.

The Clippers improved to 3-8 and dealt the Thunder their third straight defeat. Oklahoma City fell to 8-5.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

According to ClutchPoints' Tomer Azarly, the Clippers also ended their nine-game losing streak against the Thunder.

"Last LA win versus OKC was on January 16, 2024," added Azarly on X.

At that time, the Clippers still featured Kawhi Leonard, James Harden, Paul George, Russell Westbrook, Norman Powell, and Ivica Zubac.

Garland finished with 24 points, four rebounds, and seven assists, while Brook Lopez had 26 points, seven rebounds, and four assists. Derrick Jones Jr. added 14 points, five rebounds, and four blocks.

The Clippers shot 16-of-41 from long range.

Los Angeles led at halftime, 57-44. Oklahoma City, however, woke up in the third quarter, outscoring the Clippers, 40-25, to take control of the contest. Jared McCain punctuated it with a buzzer-beating three-pointer from 30 feet.

The Clippers, however, refused to fold and rallied behind Garland, Lopez, and Gradey Dick, who scored 10 points in the fourth quarter.

"I'm just proud of the guys. Got down six, I think, and then to come back and win that game is a huge win for us," said Ty Lue in the postgame conference.

articles.title: Notre Dame downs McClintock to advance in 5A football playoffs
articles.summary: Decker Haskins-Smith's three touchdowns and a stifling defense helped lead the Saints to the quarterfinals.
articles.body:
Scottsdale Notre Dame Prep Head Coach George Prelock had some concerns about whether his team would be rusty against McClintock on Friday, after the Saints went three weeks without a game.

Any such concerns were quickly put to rest in the Nov. 13 5A playoff game, as No. 3 seed Notre Dame (8-2) scored on its first drive then capitalized on Chargers' turnovers for a big second quarter en route to a 42-14 victory over No. 19 McClintock (8-4) in the second round of the 5A state playoffs at Scottsdale Notre Dame.

The Saints last played on Oct. 23. Their Oct. 30 game against Desert Mountain was canceled due to weather and last week they had a first-round playoff bye.

Early in the second quarter, with Notre Dame Prep leading 7-0, senior Matt Higby picked off a McClintock pass in Saints territory. That led to a four-yard touchdown run by Decker Haskins-Smith with 9 minutes left in the quarter to put his team ahead, 14-0.

Just 90 seconds later, the Notre Dame Prep defense picked off another McClintock pass. This time it was junior Austin Bush who got the takeaway, which led to Bush scoring a five-yard rushing touchdown.

The two defensive takeaways set the table for a 21-point second quarter that put the game out of reach for McClintock. The two takeaways were also part of seven overall on the night.

While Notre Dame Prep got key contributions from its defense, Haskins-Smith was a leader on offense. The senior had three touchdowns on the night, which included a two-yard rushing score that came with 8:21 left in the opening quarter, a four-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, and another rushing touchdown that put the Saints ahead, 42-14, with 3:14 left in the contest.

McClintock began to show signs of life late in the third quarter thanks to star Aidan Whitaker. The senior, who entered the game leading the Chargers with 17 touchdowns on the season, had an 11-yard touchdown pass to senior Jesus Otero to cut the Notre Dame Prep lead to 35-7. In the fourth quarter he had a seven-yard rushing touchdown to cut the Saints lead again, this time to 35-14.

"We really just work every day and nothing at practice stops us. We're always competing, we're a tight team, and our defense is unstoppable." - Notre Dame Prep senior Matt Higby on his team's defense

"We were just prepared and our defense is always opportunistic. When they had the opportunity to go and get the ball, they did. When they had a strip they made sure that they jumped on it. So, I'm pretty proud of how our defense played tonight. Anytime they get seven turnovers it's absolutely incredible." - Notre Dame Prep Head Coach George Prelock on his team's defense against McClintock.

Notre Dame will host No. 11 Glendale Cactus on Nov. 20 in the 5A quarterfinals. The Cobras defeated No. 6 Desert View 22-20 on Nov. 13. The teams did not meet in the regular season.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns vs. Houston Texans: 2 key matchups to watch on Sunday
articles.summary: Denzel Ward vs. Nico Collins and Denzel Boston vs. Derek Stingley Jr. outcomes could determine who goes home a winner.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans on Sunday in a game with actual playoff implications for both teams .

Cleveland is currently tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff spot in the AFC, but the Patriots hold the edge with a 5-1 record in the conference. The Browns already have three conference losses, so a fourth one on Sunday would put a major dent in their playoff hopes and also give the Texans the tiebreaker.

But if the Browns pick up the win? Then they will enter the bye week with a 45 percent chance of making the playoffs, according to The Athletic's playoff simulator , which means meaningful football will be on the docket for the rest of the season.

While much of the focus of Sunday's game will be on how Cleveland's offensive line can keep Houston's pass rush, which comes into the game tied for first in the league with 29 sacks, away from quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has taken a league-high 33 sacks, there are other matchups to watch.

Here are two in particular to keep an eye on, according to Pro Football Focus.

Houston WR Nico Collins vs. Cleveland CB Denzel Ward

Collins is second on the Texans in receptions (28), and first in receiving yards (384) and receiving touchdowns (4). But he hasn't had an explosive game since early October when he torched the Dallas Cowboys with seven receptions for 118 yards and two touchdowns.

Ward, meanwhile, is putting together his standard season of high-level play, which makes for a good matchup, according to PFF :

Collins has missed time in 2026 but has been tremendously dynamic as usual when healthy. He's notched an 82.8 PFF receiving grade along with 2.10 yards per route run, with 2026 marking his fourth straight season with numbers reaching those thresholds. Further, Collins' 82.4% contested catch rate is the third-best among receivers with 35 or more targets. Ward has starred from the outset this season, earning a 72.0-plus PFF coverage grade in all but one game throughout the year. He's permitted just 18 catches for 129 yards across 349 coverage snaps, numbers that warrant being a first-team All-Pro through the midway point of 2026. These two standouts haven't gone head-to-head in a game since the 2023 postseason, although Ward has generally had Collins' number. Collins has been held to two catches for 53 yards over their three games facing one another, with Ward winning 75% of the reps in terms of being charted as open.

articles.title: The 10 Takeaways From Canucks Quarter Season
articles.summary: The first quarter of the Vancouver Canucks season has come and gone. It has been a miserable start, with just […]
articles.body:
The first quarter of the Vancouver Canucks season has come and gone. It has been a miserable start, with just three wins in the first 21 games. It is the worst start in franchise history and also by any NHL team in the salary cap era. However, in a rebuilding season, fans and players alike are looking for positives. Rebuilds come with a lot of messy, sloppy hockey, but not all of it is discouraging.

10 Takeaways, Half Positive, Half Negative at the Quarter Mark

Positive: Jonathan Lekkerimäki 's Big Step

Maybe the greatest positive story of the season is the rise of Jonathan Lekkerimäki. It has not been a smooth path to this point, but finally, he has broken through and carved out a full-time NHL role.

Lekkerimäki was seen as one of the top prospects in the Canucks organization when he was drafted 15th overall in 2022. His professional debut for Djurgårdens IF in the SHL during the 2021–22 season was a standout campaign, where he recorded seven goals and two assists in 26 games. He became the second most-productive 17-year-old goal scorer in SHL history after Peter Forsberg , who had seven goals in 23 games.

A foot injury delayed his development in the 2022-23 season. During the 2023–24 season, he recorded a healthy 19 goals and 12 assists in 46 games. He was named the SHL Rookie of the Year and earned the Elite Prospects Award as the top SHL junior-aged player.

He left Sweden in 2024 for North America.

After getting his first NHL call-up in the 2024-25 season, Lekkerimäki showed some promise, scoring his first goal in just his second game. After that, he played the majority of his games with the Abbotsford Canucks, and won the championship in 2025. Lekkerimäki recorded seven points in 16 games through that glorious run.

Injuries hampered his 2025-26 campaign, as he suffered a shoulder injury on October 19, 2025, against the Washington Capitals. He tried to play through it, but he would have to undergo season-ending surgery in February 2026. The injury involved a combination of a torn labrum and rotator cuff damage.

This season, management and coaches were willing to give Lekkerimäki a chance at the NHL level, and he hasn't looked back. He has become a more complete player, as he has gotten stronger on puck retrievals and board battles. His lethal shot was always an asset, but he became more than just a one-dimensional producer. He is spending more time with the puck, and if he could spend more time in front of the net, his production could spike.

NOT A REPLAY! LEK WITH THE TYING GOAL! pic.twitter.com/HEGGABokcJ — Vancouver Canucks (@Canucks) October 28, 2026

NOT A REPLAY! LEK WITH THE TYING GOAL! pic.twitter.com/HEGGABokcJ

Vancouver Canucks (@Canucks) October 28, 2026

Strong work by Elias Pettersson on the boards to keep the puck in the corner until he can get help from Jonathan Lekkerimäki, then a remarkably quick release from Jake DeBrusk — so quick that none of the replays captured it. #Canucks pic.twitter.com/IRDhu0ReB2 — Daniel Wagner (@passittobulis) October 11, 2026

Strong work by Elias Pettersson on the boards to keep the puck in the corner until he can get help from Jonathan Lekkerimäki, then a remarkably quick release from Jake DeBrusk — so quick that none of the replays captured it. #Canucks pic.twitter.com/IRDhu0ReB2

Daniel Wagner (@passittobulis) October 11, 2026

At the core, the Canucks are running into talent issues, leading to losses. However, the least the team could do is show fans an honest effort. For the majority of the games, the effort was clear. Over the last couple of weeks, there have been a few poor efforts marked by lazy play. The games against the Detroit Red Wings, Winnipeg Jets, and Philadelphia Flyers come to mind, along with a lot of poor starts to games. Especially in the Philadelphia game, the Canucks had six shots through two periods. The main reason for this was players waiting for the puck to come to them instead of being assertive. The Canucks need to make the other team work for the win, and they have occasionally done that. Now, it is more about being more consistent.

Despite the record, the Canucks' goal differential is not as awful as some other rebuilding teams over the past seasons, which shows that they are not getting blown out every night. The Canucks still have the ability to hang around in games at the very least.

Positive: Willander and Pettersson Becoming Reliable Defenders

After a tough start to the season, Tom Willander is slowly becoming arguably the most reliable defenseman on the Canucks. His puck control and movement in the defensive end have been calm and collected, with cleaner breakouts. Even though he only has three assists in 16 games this season, he has established a very important role on the team.

The analytics back that up. He is second among Canucks defensemen with a 48.38 CF% (Corsi-For Percentage) in all situations, which means he is a defender who has been proficient in leading his team to generate scoring chances while giving up the least. Without Willander for the three-game stretch against the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Philadelphia Flyers, two of those games were the worst games of the season. He also has the best plus/minus stat among Canuck players who have played more than five games, at minus-one.

Tom Willander leads all #Canucks in 5v5 ice time this season Over the last 5 games, with Willander on ice: Goals: 5-5 (50%) Shots: 37-33 (52.9%) xGoals: 4.15-3.32 (55.6%) Without: Goals: 5-12 (29.4%) Shots: 34-83 (29.1%) xGoals: 3.58-8.17 (30.5%) pic.twitter.com/vzmoKbF5cn — Hamalytics (@Hamalytics) October 30, 2026

Tom Willander leads all #Canucks in 5v5 ice time this season Over the last 5 games, with Willander on ice: Goals: 5-5 (50%) Shots: 37-33 (52.9%) xGoals: 4.15-3.32 (55.6%) Without: Goals: 5-12 (29.4%) Shots: 34-83 (29.1%) xGoals: 3.58-8.17 (30.5%) pic.twitter.com/vzmoKbF5cn

Hamalytics (@Hamalytics) October 30, 2026

Elias Pettersson has also been very solid this season. He leads the Canucks with a 48.70 CF%, and much like Willander, he has looked calm and collected with the puck. He also has some underrated offensive capabilities, as his offensive awareness has been impressive to watch at times. With a contract extension needed at the end of this season, his play early on this season may have earned him a hefty raise. It would be in the Canucks' best interest to get a contract done with him quickly.

ON A PLATTER. 🍽️ Perfect pass from Chytil to D-Petey! pic.twitter.com/2PQ42D2Dik — Vancouver Canucks (@Canucks) October 15, 2026

ON A PLATTER. 🍽️ Perfect pass from Chytil to D-Petey! pic.twitter.com/2PQ42D2Dik

Vancouver Canucks (@Canucks) October 15, 2026

Negative: Penalty Kill Gives Up Chances Too Easily

The Canucks rank last in the NHL on the penalty kill at 62.7%. That comes as no surprise, as the defensemen are constantly too puck-focused. It leads to the team chasing the puck, while not getting proper body and stick position against opponents. Much of that is due to a lack of experience, especially in the case of Zeev Buium and D-Petey, but veterans are also struggling to keep up as opponents are skating circles around the Canucks.

To find a positive in a negative, Elias Pettersson , the forward, has only surrendered four power-play goals in over 45 minutes of PK time. So, he is certainly not the problem. We are not here to point fingers, as Malhotra would say, but the biggest things to improve are blocking the cross-seam passes and the low-to-high passes to the bumper and to the middle of the ice. Perhaps, deploying other players on the penalty kill would be a worthy experiment.

I do not want to clog this piece with clips, so if you want to see some examples of how the Canucks have struggled with low-to-high coverage, check out my postgame analysis of the Canucks against the Anaheim Ducks .

Positive: Pettersson Re-Discovering His Game

Arguably, the biggest story from the Canucks this season has been the resurgence of Elias Pettersson. Following two seasons of lackluster play under Rick Tocchet and Adam Foote , the new management and environment have brought better play out of him. He is still far from what he was in his first five and a half seasons, but his confidence has returned. He is willing to make the dekes and, most importantly, the one-timers. His foot speed and shot are still not what they looked like at his peak, and his five-on-five production is still virtually nonexistent, but to be at a point-per-game pace on a rebuilding team is some good work.

This is the coolest thing Pettersson has done in years. #Canucks pic.twitter.com/8smt5Aoqpt — Daniel Wagner (@passittobulis) October 30, 2026

This is the coolest thing Pettersson has done in years. #Canucks pic.twitter.com/8smt5Aoqpt

Daniel Wagner (@passittobulis) October 30, 2026

He also continues to be a balanced player, and even has a bit of a physical edge this season. His hit averages have definitely dropped off after the first few games, but he is still willing to be physical when necessary. He also blocks shots and is a solid penalty killer. It will be interesting if his engagement level stays consistent throughout the balance of this season as losses keep piling up.

Negative: The Concerning Play of Kevin Lankinen

Kevin Lankinen has played with a messy defensive structure in front of him this season. In that kind of environment, pretty much any goalie will have some below-average numbers. However, I do not know if anyone expected it to be nearly as bad as it is for him.

It has been a snowball effect for Lankinen this season. He was pulled twice in the span of a week early in the season, and has never recovered since then. Both Lankinen and Leevi Meriläinen are very active goalies, but Lankinen has overplayed his position much more often. As Ray Ferraro said on the broadcast of November 3rd's game against Anaheim, Lankinen looks like he is "guessing" in the crease. It is a sign that his confidence is low right now. He does not trust his reads, and the defense cannot do much to bail him out either.

We have talked at length about a buyout possibility for Lankinen , and frankly, it would not be a smart move, given how the goaltending position is the most volatile in the NHL. By the time the Canucks are competitive again, the team would not want to be hemorrhaging cap space on players no longer with the organization. The only thing they can do right now is let Lankinen play through his struggles. However, Meriläinen's solid play early in the season will make it difficult for Lankinen to get any run of games. Lankinen will have to earn his keep.

Positive: Management is Staying the Course, Malhotra's Solid Leadership

It is clear that Ryan Johnson and the Sedins have a good understanding of what a rebuild entails. They are not making any panic moves, such as trades or calling prospects like Braeden Cootes or Adam Novotny up. In an interview on Donnie & Dhali earlier in the season, Johnson remained steadfast in staying the course. While some may lobby for Cootes to get called up for a look, Johnson made it clear in the interview that he will not rush Cootes' development.

"I want him to experience everything and anything he can at the American Hockey League level before he comes here. There's no question he's gonna be a part of this organization for a long time and a big part of the turnaround here… I just want to be very strategic about when that is," said Johnson.

As the Canucks are going through rough times, now would be the worst time to bring the young kids up, especially when Abbotsford is thriving. Johnson understands the situation, and although losing regularly is tough, he has not lost sight of the long-term process.

Takeaways From the Sedins' Press Conference

On Thursday this week, the Sedins addressed the media, optimistic but committed to the rebuild. Both Sedins talked about how they could have opted for a retool and sold the fans on it, but the goal is not simply to make the Stanley Cup Playoffs, but to do it consistently. Short-term pain is needed for long-term gain. However, the quote that stood out from that press conference is the idea of not simply trading away veterans for draft picks, emphasizing a need to insulate young players with seasoned players.

"We're not going to trade away players just to get more draft picks," said Henrik. "You also need to put a better product on the ice." Daniel also added that draft picks alone would not get them through a rebuild.

It is clear that management is trying to cater to both sides of the fanbase: fans who are more focused on the idea of rebuilding, and the fans who want to enjoy watching the Canucks, day in and day out, who want to see a good team on the ice. Both sides of the fanbase are important, and getting a reasonable level of attendance at Rogers Arena is critical for revenue. It is a delicate balance, though the downplaying of draft picks may be a concern to some. The mindset is understandable, and we will see what the moves look like going forward before we make any judgments. However, patience among a lot of the fanbase has worn thin, understandably so.

Malhotra, the Honorary Captain of the Ship?

Head Coach Manny Malhotra has shown that he is like the captain of the ship while the team opted to go without one this year. Players listen to him, and while it is way too early to assess if Malhotra is a good coach, he has been a calming presence with his demeanour. One thing that is mildly concerning, however, is the lineup deployment as of late. Filip Hronek recorded over 31 minutes against Philadelphia on November 9; both Elias Pettersson (the forward) and Filip Chytil have trended way above the 20-minute mark in recent outings, and Leevi Meriläinen has started seven of the last eight games. Clearly, for morale's sake, Malhotra is trying to do everything he can to get a win for his team, but for the sake of the long-term picture, he may need to steel himself even in losses and stay more balanced in deployment.

Now, the concern here goes a few ways. On one hand, you have Brendan Gallagher and Luke Schenn , two players who were brought in to be leaders and improve the culture. From what we have seen of them, they have indeed been good leaders in the dressing room. However, both players have been largely non-factors on the ice. Gallagher has two points in 17 games and just under 11 minutes of ice time per game on average. He has looked slow, although he still works hard. Age is certainly catching up to him, as is the case with Schenn, who has only played 12 games this season. Schenn's ice time is quickly diminishing too, as he only logged 8:17 in the game against Philadelphia on November 9. Malhotra's faith in Schenn is clearly wavering. However, this is not really the key concern here.

O'Connor and Rossi Are the Bigger Concerns

It is the play of Drew O'Connor and Marco Rossi that is of greater concern. O'Connor has just five points on the season and a minus-10 rating through 21 games. He also has 18 penalty minutes, leading the team in minor penalties taken. Malhotra called out O'Connor for his penalties because it is especially frustrating that a player known for his speed has to resort to trips and hooks to try and win puck battles.

As for Rossi, he is younger, but as he has played over 250 games, we will call him a veteran. He has not scored since the second game of the season, and his ice time has dropped as a result. It has gone down to as low as 12 minutes on November 9. Malhotra mentioned that he has to get inside more, rather than being a perimeter player. He has created chances and has the fifth-most shots on the team, but his shooting percentage is down significantly this season, from 20.5% last season to 8.6% this season.

Positive: Community Involvement Has Returned to Form

The final positive takeaway from the first quarter of the season is from off the ice. Through the first month and a half of the season, the Canucks have been much more involved in the community. It came as a mandate of sorts from the Sedins and Johnson that the team would get out into the community and be ambassadors of the sport. So far, they have lived up to that promise. The Canucks have been out and about at the fire department in Penticton, B.C. Children's Hospital, the Ronald McDonald House, Canuck Place and more.

articles.title: BMW "proud of what we achieved" after securing runner-up in 2026 WEC
articles.summary: BMW wrapped up the season with second in the WEC manufacturers' standings, but ran into a familiar technical headache in the Monza finale
articles.body:
BMW says it can be "proud" of its results in the 2026 World Endurance Championship after finishing second in the manufacturers' standings, despite failing to mount a sustained title challenge to Toyota.

Kevin, Magnussen, Raffaele Marciello and Dries Vanthoor ended an eventful Monza 6 Hours in fifth in the #15 BMW M Hybrid V8, while the sister #20 entry shared by Rene Rast, Robin Frijns and Sheldon van der Linde was classified in seventh.

Reflecting on a campaign that featured two victories and three further podium finishes in Hypercar, BMW motorsport boss Andreas Roos said that the 2026 season finale provided a positive conclusion.

"In the last years, we came back into [the top class of] sports car racing for BMW for the first time since 1999," Roos said.

"And now fighting with Toyota, which is in the championship without any break since 2012, I think it's a great achievement and we can be proud.

"It's a big thank you to everybody who is involved from the team, the drivers, also all the people in Munich at BMW Motorsport who work so hard every single day to get this forward.

"The fact that both cars went into the finale level on points underlines just how evenly matched and strong both crews are. We can build on that. We are looking forward to the new season and want to come back even stronger to fight for victory at Le Mans and for the world championship."

WRT team principal Vincent Vosse echoed those thoughts, claiming that while the team always targets titles, finishing second and third in such a fiercely contested world championship is a very good result.

In Sunday's six-hour finale, after a difficult qualifying session, both BMW M Hybrid V8s made remarkable comebacks in the race. The #15 had to overcome a drive-through penalty for overtaking under VSC conditions and a late spin that might have cost a possible fourth-place.

"It was a wild race with plenty of ups and downs for us. Unfortunately, I received a drive-through penalty for overtaking under yellow flags, but my team-mates did an excellent job of making up for it," Magnussen said.

"We came here to secure second place in the manufacturers' standings and third place in the drivers' standings. We achieved both. We can therefore be very satisfied with the season."

Marciello admitted to mixed emotions after BMW's world championship aspirations fell through due to difficult races in Austin and Barcelona when main rival Toyota scored big.

"Considering where we started, this is a very good result at Monza. Second place in the manufacturers' standings is a great result, as is third place in the drivers' standings," the Swiss-Italian said.

#15 BMW M Team WRT BMW M Hybrid V8: Kevin Magnussen, Raffaele Marciello, Dries Vanthoor

"However, I have mixed feelings because, when you have been fighting for the title for so long, you get used to being in that position and are a little disappointed when you ultimately fall just short."

Another braking problem for the M Hybrid V8

The #20 car BMW shared by Frijns, Rast and Van der Linde enjoyed an even stronger run early on at Monza, running in the podium positions for a time before a familiar technical bug reared its head.

Once more a BMW Hybrid V8 ran into braking troubles, leading to multiple lock-ups for Frijns and even dropping the car out of the points. Late-race penalties and accidents for rivals elevated the #20 back to seventh in the official result.

"We had some technical issues on car #20 that we need to analyse. It is linked to the hybrid, but exactly where and how [we don't know]," Vosse said.

"Of course, it has an impact on braking inconsistency. We could see it coming, and while our strategy was going well and the pace was strong, it got worse toward the end."

It is the second time this year that the braking problems, which plagued the car way back in its infancy, returned with the 2026 evo version after WRT lost a possible victory at the Road America IMSA race back in August due to a braking failure. It is still unclear whether those issues are related.

#20 BMW M Team WRT BMW M Hybrid V8: Rene Rast, Robin Frijns

Rast shared his frustration over the lost opportunity, losing a possible podium and maybe even a chance of a race victory.

"The race started well. At one stage, we were on course for the podium, but we encountered some technical problems in the closing stages that dropped us back. That is a shame because we deserved a podium finish," the German said.

"Nevertheless, we can be satisfied overall with our successes and the progress we made this season. We can build on that and hopefully do even better next year."

BMW's factory partner WRT achieved a remarkable result as well by scoring a win with all of its four cars across the two classes.

Meanwhile, Roos already made a strong statement for 2027: "We did not achieve our main objective: we wanted to fight at the very front both at Le Mans and in the World Championship. Unfortunately, we did not manage to do that. For 2027, we want to improve further so that we can compete at the very front."

articles.title: Joe Burrow’s MVP hype gets an unexpected backer
articles.summary: The Bengals QB is winning critics over with his stunning pace.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is (somehow) quietly shooting up the projected MVP charts.

The running tally so far? Eight games, 74 percent completion percentage, 2,386 yards, 23 touchdowns and just six interceptions for a 6-2 team hoping to make it 7-2 and tops in the AFC North with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night.

The MVP pace is getting hard to deny, to the point even a consistent Bengals critic like Night Wright is coming around to the idea for Burrow.

"I think [Joe Burrow] is going to end up being the MVP this year," Wright said on First Things First. "The numbers are outstanding, the remaining schedule is soft… I think the Bengals are gonna have a really good record, he's going to have plenty of opportunity to put up stats."

It's not just the obvious stuff, either. Burrow's averaging 2.118 touchdown passes per game, the highest in NFL history:

Burrow is currently on pace for 49 touchdowns and 5,000-plus yards, among other eye-popping numbers. Things need to keep going right, especially with the rather unusual healthy streak for his top wideouts and entire offensive line, but the numbers could be pretty undeniable.

Don't forget, too, that the Bengals will face a pretty "easy" schedule the rest of the way, so the winning part of the MVP conversation could shape up nicely for Burrow, too.

articles.title: FAA ground stop throws college football into chaos, while the NFL is safe
articles.summary: A Federal Aviation Administration ground stop that lasted more than four hours and canceled over 7,000 flights Friday affected the travel plans for several pro and college teams across multiple sports.
articles.body: A Federal Aviation Administration ground stop that lasted more than four hours and canceled over 7,000 flights Friday affected the travel plans for several teams across multiple sports. Follow along for live coverage. Multiple games in college football had to be rescheduled to accommodate new travel plans, while a handful of NBA teams changed their flights as a result of the ground stop. Every NFL game, meanwhile, will be played as scheduled, as all road teams were scheduled to travel Saturday. A few backup referees for the NFL Every NFL game will stick to its original start time, a league spokesman confirmed to NBC News. Teams playing Sunday typically do not travel until Saturday, meaning the league was largely unaffected by the Friday ground stop. The New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions, who are playing in Munich, Germany, both traveled overseas well ahead of the stop. While the league’s teams and players will arrive as scheduled, the NFL did have to modify officiating crews for Sunday’s games. “Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns,” a league spokesman said. Three backup referees — Duane Heydt, Barry Anderson and Don Willard — will be used Sunday. Heydt was assigned to a game in New Orleans and Anderson to one in Tennessee, while Willard will be the side judge for games in both Indianapolis and Cincinnati. (The kickoffs in those two games are more than seven hours apart, and the stadiums are separated by less than 120 miles.) “Each of the league’s 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise,” the league spokesman said. Many college football games have been pushed back Travel plans for more than a dozen teams were affected by the stoppage, according to The Athletic. Some schools opted to fly out on Saturday morning for games scheduled the same day, while others — including the Alabama Crimson Tide playing at Vanderbilt — took a bus to their destination. Several kickoffs were pushed back to later Saturday to accommodate new travel plans, including the games between Baylor and BYU, Arizona State and UCF, and Utah and Arizona. The game between Oklahoma and Ole Miss, however, was pushed back to Sunday after Ole Miss couldn’t figure out its travel in time — and it drew a strong response from the Sooners. “We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned. But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution,” Oklahoma Athletic Director Roger Denny said in a statement. “After multiple conversations with the league office, [SEC] Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection. After continued discussions, he further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit.” Denny’s statement added: “Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans. Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference’s decision tonight.” No major issues for the NBA and NHL A few NBA teams — such as the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Chicago Bulls — had to reschedule flights from Friday night to Saturday morning, but otherwise it’s largely business as usual for the league. An NBA source confirmed to NBC News all games would take place as scheduled as of Saturday morning, though noted there were a lot of moving parts. “Flights are late, get stuck on the runway, just like it does in the normal commercial world of flight, so it’s just part of it,” Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson said before the team’s game Friday. “We’ve all been part of it. You just adapt.” Atkinson’s star guard Donovan Mitchell was not enthused about the new plan, as Cleveland has a quick turnaround to another game Saturday. “This is unprecedented,” Mitchell said Friday, per Cleveland.com’s Chris Fedor. “Back-to-back. Three-hour flight. It was already going to be a tough one. But if they say we have to play then we have to play.” Mitchell added he would have liked for the game to be canceled. The NHL, meanwhile, has not announced any changes to its schedule. The league had only two games on Friday night, allowing most teams to travel for their road games prior to the stoppage, according to The Athletic.

articles.title: El Pons Lleida da la campanada ante el Barça y buscará su primera Copa Continental
articles.standfirst: Será la segunda ocasión en la que dispute el partido por el título tras la final de 2021. Se enfrentará al Oporto, vigente campeón de Europa
articles.summary: Será la segunda ocasión en la que dispute el partido por el título tras la final de 2021. Se enfrentará al Oporto, vigente campeón de Europa
articles.body: El Pons Lleida protagonizó este sábado la gran sorpresa de la Copa Continental al eliminar al Barça, el equipo más laureado de la competición con 18 títulos, en una semifinal disputada en el pabellón Joan Ortoll de Calafell que enloqueció tras el descanso y acabó con diez goles en la segunda mitad (6-5). Liderado por Sebastià Moncusí y Jordi Badia, autores de sendos dobletes, el cuadro ilerdense castigó los errores de un Barça que parecía tener el partido bajo control, pero que terminó pagando su falta de contundencia defensiva. No es la primera vez que el conjunto catalán pelea por este trofeo, ya que disputó la final en 2021, aunque entonces cayó ante el Sporting de Lisboa (3-1). De hecho, el equipo azulgrana se marchó al descanso con ventaja gracias a un tanto de Ignacio Alabart (1-0). Sin embargo, la segunda mitad dio un vuelco al encuentro. Jordi Badia culminó la remontada con el 3-2 y obligó al Barça a remar a contracorriente. Martí Casas restableció la igualdad (3-3), pero Sebastià Moncusí y el argentino Fabrizio Ciocale dispararon al Lleida hasta el 5-3 a tres del final.. Con todo, el Barça no había dicho su última palabra. Nico Ojeda, que se enfrentaba a su exequipo, recortó distancias a menos de dos minutos del final (5-4), pero el Lleida resistió el asedio. Con la portería azulgrana desguarnecida, Àlex Ortigosa sentenció a 23 segundos de la conclusión (6-4). El tanto de Martí Casas sobre la bocina solo sirvió para maquillar el resultado definitivo. articles.title: Spirit come back to beat Royals 2-1, securing a place in the NWSL Championship at home
articles.summary: The Washington Spirit became the NWSL’s first team to reach five championship games (without relocation involved) Saturday after a 2-1 win over the seventh-s...
articles.body:
The Washington Spirit became the NWSL's first team to reach five championship games (without relocation involved) Saturday after a 2-1 win over the seventh-seed Utah Royals, who braved a thunderous Audi Field in their first-ever playoff appearance.

After the Royals took an early lead in the second minute on an Olimpico from Cloé Lacasse that shocked the crowd, Washington responded with an equalizer — a tap-in from Sofia Cantore — that showcased the squad's depth. Spirit striker Clara Luvanga pounced on the Royals' defensive mistake and scored the game-winner.

The Spirit have reached the last two NWSL championships and lost both. On Saturday afternoon, they overcame a near scheduling snafu, football lines and a far sterner defensive test than their quarterfinal against the Portland Thorns last week to return to the final — one they will host at Audi Field next weekend.

From the star of the semifinal to Utah's run coming to a close, the first semifinal of the weekend offered plenty of entertainment. The Athletic breaks down how it happened.

Luvanga's invaluable (and multifaceted) impact

Luvanga's winning goal for the Spirit marked the second consecutive time she's pounced on a defensive error and punished her opponents. Last week, the Tanzanian international picked the ball from Thorns goalkeeper Mackenzie Arnold. On Saturday, she did it to Royals fullback Nuria Rábano, who under-hit a pass back to goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn. Luvanga happily intercepted it in the 56th minute to give the Spirit their first lead.

The sequence illustrated how tight the margins were in this semifinal and how little they can be for Luvanga to make a difference. The 21-year-old has now had four goals and three assists since her first appearance for the Spirit on Sept. 26, and there is still a strong sense that she's in warm-up mode.

Luvanga's performance wasn't perfect. The Royals' early goal came from a corner kick that slipped through Lacasse's legs as she attempted to guard the near post, but Luvanga's positives far outweighed that eighth-minute slip-up. Her hold-up play allowed Trinity Rodman to make the wide run that led to Cantore's goal, and she delivered an exquisite cross with the outside of her foot in the second half to midfielder Melissa Bethi. Officials recalled the goal because Luvanga was offside in the buildup, but such is the warm-up nature of her game. For a player like Luvanga, that will probably be a goal next time. — Tamerra Griffin

An Olimpico and Tanaka's return not enough for the Royals

Utah came into Audi with a game plan after probably watching tape from last weekend's quarterfinal romp when the Spirit dominated the Portland Thorns in a 4-1 win. The challenge is turning the intellectual understanding of a Rodman-Luvanga-Sofia Cantore frontline into a full 90 minutes of defending. While they gave Rodman perhaps a bit too much respect on the Spirit's first goal by allowing her to make a run, they got the rest of that play right. Cantore crashing the box and pushing the ball with physicality and placement was too much.

So it's understandable that the Royals left Audi feeling like they could have stolen that semifinal from the Spirit, but were undone by a single back pass. After last week, however, a mistake like that feels unforgivable.

Even with Mina Tanaka taking the pitch for the final 30 minutes, a win was already out of reach for the Royals. The Spirit forced them to defend wave after wave, and Utah couldn't draw up anything truly dangerous from direct play. At least it can walk away with Lacasse's Olimpico in the first five minutes as a brief moment of joy.

The Royals exit the playoffs after a remarkable 2026, and a statement upset win in the quarterfinals over the San Diego Wave. — Meg Linehan

The football lines for the semifinal were unavoidable as soon as the Spirit successfully forced their way back into Audi Field for the match, resulting in a doubleheader with the Secretaries' Cup (a Division III football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the U.S. Coast Guard Academy). The football lines were a temporary annoyance, and to be fair, the field crew went all in on making those yellow lines visible for the Spirit. Sure, it was a throwback to the NWSL's early days, but it could be a one-off problem, and one the league won't mind (assuming those lines are fully scrubbed by next Saturday).

The bigger issue to monitor is the state of the pitch itself. Between the square patch of questionable-looking grass in the six-yard box at the supporters group end, and the general patchiness, combine 90 minutes of football with a full game of the other football … well. It might not be great, to say the least. — Linehan

The Spirit will await the winner of Gotham FC versus Kansas City Current on Sunday to determine who their opponent in the NWSL Championship on Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET at Audi Field.

articles.title: Former Arizona WR Braylen Ross flipped his commitment to Oklahoma State
articles.summary: Irvine (Calif.) Crean Lutheran wide-out Braylen Ross has flipped his commitment from Arizona to Oklahoma State.
articles.body:
Irvine (Calif.) Crean Lutheran wide-out Braylen Ross has flipped his commitment from Arizona to Oklahoma State .

Ross committed to the Wildcats back in May but took an official visit to Oklahoma State over Halloween weekend. He told us he loved everything about the visit, felt at home and decided to flip his commitment to the Cowboys earlier today.

"I fell in love with the school on that visit," Ross said. "I loved everything about it and obviously really like the football program. They have a great offense that features the passing game and I think it's a great all around fit for me.

"I was there for Homecoming weekend and the game atmosphere and fan support were incredible. That visit really opened my eyes and exceeded my expectations. I had never been to a game and seen fan support like that. It was honestly like nothing I've ever seen before."

Ross said his relationship with the coaches played a big role.

"I really like the coaching staff," Ross said. "They made me feel like I was a high priority ever since they offered me back in September. I felt a really strong connection with everyone there and especially Coach Morris and Coach Edwards.

"It wasn't an easy decision, and these types of things are never easy. I had a lot of respect for the Arizona staff, but I really felt like this was the best decision for me and I'm looking forward to becoming a college athlete at Oklahoma State."

Ross had a breakout season at Crean Lutheran after transferring in from San Diego (Calif.) Lincoln over the Spring. He had to sit out his junior season at Lincoln due to some eligibility issues but flashed at several camps and 7v7 events and looked primed for a strong senior year.

"I know there are some guys rated higher but for me, he's not just one of the best receivers in California; he's one of the best in the entire region, Malik James of James Sports Group said. "He's tall, he's physical, has big hands, has a high end skill set, and great body control.

"On top of that, he's a great kid with a great personality. "I like everything about him and I think he's a great pickup for Oklahoma State."

articles.title: Chargers' offensive keys to victory against the Ravens
articles.summary: Here's what the Los Angeles Chargers need to do on offense to pull out the win in Week 10.
articles.body:
The 0-8 Chargers are on national television this week as they continue searching for their first win, hoping former defensive coordinator Jesse Minter will deliver it.

Here's what the Chargers need to do on offense to come away with a win Monday night against the Ravens .

Los Angeles snapped a 37-drive streak without a touchdown last week against Houston in the fourth quarter, but much of that streak overlapped with wide receiver Ladd McConkey's absence. With McConkey out last week due to pregame back spasms that also kept him from practicing Thursday and Friday, the Chargers have to prove their other weapons can threaten an NFL-caliber defense. That'll start with those pieces getting healthy themselves - running back Keaton Mitchell (hip), wide receivers Tre' Harris (shoulder) and Brenen Thompson (hamstring), and tight end David Njoku (fibula) were all on the injury report on Thursday alongside McConkey.

Herbert was sacked a career-high 8 times last week against the Texans , which culminated in a finger injury on his left hand that brought him out of a game that had already been decided. Herbert is good to go this week, so the Chargers need to do better against a Ravens pass rush that has struggled to get off the ground this season, as no Baltimore defender has more than 3 sacks this year. Again, that story will start with health - right guard Cole Strange will likely start despite being benched last week because both of his backups, Branson Taylor and rookie Alex Harkey, landed on the injury report. Los Angeles is still working to get guard Kayode Awosika and swing lineman Trey Pipkins III back from their own injuries as well.

The Chargers have turned the ball over multiple times in five consecutive games and lead the league with 19 total giveaways. It's getting old to keep making this a point of emphasis for the offense, but until LA can get through a game without handing the ball to the other team, it remains worth harping on. Herbert is the only quarterback in the league to throw an interception in all eight of his team's games this season, but the Chargers have also struggled with ball security. It will need to tighten up for Los Angeles to have a fighting chance.

In their last four games, the Ravens have been outscored 84-10 in the second half, an encouraging sign for the Chargers, since their best offensive quarter is usually the third. The Chargers are 17th in EPA/play coming out of the halftime locker room, a fairly respectable number, but they fall back to worst in the league in the fourth quarter. If they can sustain some of that third-quarter success and keep the pressure on a Ravens team that has run out of gas in recent weeks, they might slide past Baltimore and into the win column.
